metadata.historicalScope: Selected developments from c. 1850 BCE to 2024 CE
metadata.description: One shared chronology with parallel mathematical and physical subjects, point events, qualified dates and explicit connections.
metadata.namingPolicy: English prose and labels; personal names retain original-language standardized spellings or documented professional forms. Lookup aliases are provided separately.

edgeSemantics.sequence: Editorial reading order inside one subject, not a causal or exclusive intellectual lineage. Same-year ordering does not imply month-level precision.
edgeSemantics.reference: A labeled mathematical application, experimental test, transmission, reformulation or explicitly qualified comparison. See the linked events' sources.

nineteenth.title: Fields, structures, energy and rigorous analysis

foundations.title: Relativity, quantum theory and mathematical foundations

moscow-papyrus.title: The Moscow mathematical papyrus
moscow-papyrus.define: Problems include the volume of a truncated square pyramid. Practical calculation, training and geometry were already intertwined, although a modern deductive proof cannot simply be read into the surviving procedure.
moscow-papyrus.subject: geometry
moscow-papyrus.precision: Approximate manuscript date, not a precise year of discovery. The chart locates this event by year, not by an assumed 1 January date.

old-babylonian.title: Old Babylonian problem solving
old-babylonian.define: Surviving tablets record place-value sexagesimal calculation, reciprocals and procedures for problems now expressed as quadratic equations. This is evidence of scribal practices, not of modern symbolic algebra or a single inventor.
old-babylonian.subject: algebra
old-babylonian.precision: Approximate period represented by surviving tablets; this point does not date the invention of mathematics. The chart locates this event by year, not by an assumed 1 January date.

plimpton.title: Plimpton 322: right-triangle numbers
plimpton.define: This Old Babylonian tablet preserves numerical relations associated with right triangles. Its teaching or computational purpose remains debated; calling it a modern trigonometric table would overstate the evidence.
plimpton.subject: geometry
plimpton.precision: Approximate Old Babylonian date; interpretation is contested. The chart locates this event by year, not by an assumed 1 January date.

rhind-papyrus.title: The Rhind mathematical papyrus
rhind-papyrus.define: The surviving copy presents fraction arithmetic, distribution and measurement problems, drawing on an older textual tradition. Its unit-fraction methods belong to a different numerical notation from modern decimal calculation.
rhind-papyrus.subject: algebra
rhind-papyrus.precision: Approximate copying date; some underlying material is older. The chart locates this event by year, not by an assumed 1 January date.

thales.title: Θαλῆς: early geometrical traditions
thales.fullTitle: Θαλῆς and early Greek geometrical traditions
thales.define: Later sources associate Θαλῆς with geometrical results and an eclipse prediction. These retrospective accounts document a tradition of attribution; they do not establish the methods or exact dates of individual proofs.
thales.subject: geometry
thales.precision: Traditional eclipse year used as a reading landmark; mathematical attributions are retrospective. The chart locates this event by year, not by an assumed 1 January date.

pythagorean.title: Pythagorean ratios and geometry
pythagorean.fullTitle: Early Pythagorean mathematics and musical ratios
pythagorean.define: Greek traditions linked whole-number ratios, musical intervals and geometrical reasoning. The familiar right-triangle theorem was known numerically elsewhere earlier; surviving evidence does not justify assigning its first discovery to one person.
pythagorean.subject: geometry
pythagorean.precision: Approximate fifth-century BCE setting; authorship and chronology are uncertain. The chart locates this event by year, not by an assumed 1 January date.

hippocrates.title: Ἱπποκράτης: quadrature of lunes
hippocrates.fullTitle: Ἱπποκράτης and the quadrature of lunes
hippocrates.define: Work on curved figures showed that selected lunes could be related exactly to rectilinear areas. The result was narrower than squaring the circle, but helped make transformation and proof central to Greek geometry.
hippocrates.subject: geometry
hippocrates.precision: Approximate working date reconstructed from later testimony. The chart locates this event by year, not by an assumed 1 January date.

eudoxus.title: Εὔδοξος: proportion and exhaustion
eudoxus.fullTitle: Εὔδοξος develops ratio theory and exhaustion
eudoxus.define: A theory of proportion accommodated magnitudes without assuming all lengths were commensurable. Exhaustion arguments compared areas and volumes through increasingly fine bounds, anticipating some problems later treated by analysis.
eudoxus.subject: geometry
eudoxus.precision: Approximate fourth-century BCE work; later textual transmission preserves the evidence. The chart locates this event by year, not by an assumed 1 January date.

aristotle.title: Ἀριστοτέλης: motion and natural philosophy
aristotle.fullTitle: Ἀριστοτέλης systematizes motion and natural explanation
aristotle.define: His natural philosophy organized questions about change, place and celestial motion. It shaped later debate for centuries, but its categories should not be treated as an early statement of Newtonian mechanics.
aristotle.subject: motion
aristotle.precision: Approximate composition period; the works are not a single dated publication. The chart locates this event by year, not by an assumed 1 January date.

euclid.title: Εὐκλείδης: deductive geometry
euclid.define: The Elements assembled definitions, postulates and propositions into a systematic deductive presentation. Its influence concerns the organization of proof as well as geometry; the compilation incorporated earlier mathematical work.
euclid.subject: geometry
euclid.precision: Conventional approximate date of compilation. The chart locates this event by year, not by an assumed 1 January date.

archimedes-statics.title: Ἀρχιμήδης: equilibrium and levers
archimedes-statics.fullTitle: Ἀρχιμήδης studies equilibrium and centers of gravity
archimedes-statics.define: Geometrical reasoning supported propositions about levers and equilibrium. These works connect mathematical proof with idealized physical systems, without implying that every proposition was derived directly from experiment.
archimedes-statics.subject: motion
archimedes-statics.precision: Approximate period of work; individual treatise dates are uncertain. The chart locates this event by year, not by an assumed 1 January date.

archimedes-circle.title: Ἀρχιμήδης: bounds for the circle ratio
archimedes-circle.fullTitle: Ἀρχιμήδης bounds the circumference of a circle
archimedes-circle.define: Inscribed and circumscribed polygons produced rigorous upper and lower bounds for the circle ratio. The method made approximation compatible with proof, rather than identifying a finite decimal value as exact.
archimedes-circle.subject: analysis
archimedes-circle.precision: Approximate period; ordered here as a separate mathematical achievement. The chart locates this event by year, not by an assumed 1 January date.

archimedes-buoyancy.title: Ἀρχιμήδης: floating bodies
archimedes-buoyancy.fullTitle: Ἀρχιμήδης develops a theory of floating bodies
archimedes-buoyancy.define: The surviving treatise relates equilibrium to displaced fluid and investigates floating shapes. The famous bath anecdote is not required as evidence for the mathematical content of the work.
archimedes-buoyancy.subject: motion
archimedes-buoyancy.precision: Approximate treatise date; anecdotal discovery stories are not used as chronology. The chart locates this event by year, not by an assumed 1 January date.

eratosthenes.title: Ἐρατοσθένης: measuring Earth
eratosthenes.fullTitle: Ἐρατοσθένης estimates the size of Earth
eratosthenes.define: A geometrical argument combined a difference in solar altitude with an estimated terrestrial distance. The result illustrates how measurement and assumptions about shape can jointly support an inference about an inaccessible scale.
eratosthenes.subject: cosmos
eratosthenes.precision: Approximate date; the length of the ancient stadium and numerical accuracy are debated. The chart locates this event by year, not by an assumed 1 January date.

apollonius.title: Ἀπολλώνιος: conic sections
apollonius.fullTitle: Ἀπολλώνιος develops the theory of conic sections
apollonius.define: A systematic investigation of ellipses, parabolas and hyperbolas supplied a durable body of geometry. Their later role in orbital mechanics was a new application, not the original purpose of every proposition.
apollonius.subject: geometry
apollonius.precision: Approximate composition period. The chart locates this event by year, not by an assumed 1 January date.

hipparchus.title: Ἵππαρχος: quantitative astronomy
hipparchus.define: Work on chords, solar and lunar models and observations increased the mathematical precision of astronomy. Much of the evidence survives through later authors, so reconstructions of particular tables require caution.
hipparchus.subject: cosmos
hipparchus.precision: Approximate period of activity rather than a uniquely dated table. The chart locates this event by year, not by an assumed 1 January date.

nine-chapters.title: The Nine Chapters: a mathematical synthesis
nine-chapters.fullTitle: The Nine Chapters consolidate Chinese mathematical procedures
nine-chapters.define: This layered text organizes problems involving taxation, surveying, proportions and systems of linear equations. Counting-rod procedures and practical settings belong to a long textual tradition rather than a single moment of invention.
nine-chapters.subject: algebra
nine-chapters.precision: Approximate compilation landmark; material accumulated over earlier centuries. The chart locates this event by year, not by an assumed 1 January date.

ptolemy.title: Κλαύδιος Πτολεμαῖος: planetary models
ptolemy.define: The Almagest developed predictive geometrical models and a table of chords. Its mathematical success in calculation should be distinguished from accepting its geocentric physical framework today.
ptolemy.subject: cosmos
ptolemy.precision: Approximate date of the astronomical synthesis. The chart locates this event by year, not by an assumed 1 January date.

diophantus.title: Διόφαντος: arithmetic equations
diophantus.define: The Arithmetica explored selected problems through sophisticated symbolic abbreviations and rational solutions. It did not state the modern general theory of integer equations later associated with his name.
diophantus.subject: algebra
diophantus.precision: Conventional approximate third-century date; biography is poorly documented. The chart locates this event by year, not by an assumed 1 January date.

liu-hui.title: 劉徽: commentary on the Nine Chapters
liu-hui.fullTitle: 劉徽 comments on the Nine Chapters
liu-hui.define: The commentary explains algorithms through geometrical reasoning and refines polygonal approximation of the circle ratio. It records an identifiable authorial intervention within a much older mathematical tradition.
liu-hui.subject: geometry
liu-hui.precision: Dated commentary; the underlying compilation is older. The chart locates this event by year, not by an assumed 1 January date.

pappus.title: Πάππος: the Mathematical Collection
pappus.define: The Collection preserved and extended earlier Greek geometry, including discussions of loci and methods of analysis. Its later influence depended on manuscript survival, translation and reinterpretation.
pappus.subject: geometry
pappus.precision: Approximate early fourth-century compilation. The chart locates this event by year, not by an assumed 1 January date.

zu-pi.title: 祖沖之: precise bounds for the circle ratio
zu-pi.fullTitle: 祖沖之 obtains exceptionally close bounds for the circle ratio
zu-pi.define: Later records attribute bounds between 3.1415926 and 3.1415927 and the approximation 355/113 to 祖沖之. The detailed original derivation has not survived, so reconstruction should not be presented as a preserved proof.
zu-pi.subject: analysis
zu-pi.precision: Approximate fifth-century landmark; results are known through later records. The chart locates this event by year, not by an assumed 1 January date.

aryabhata.title: आर्यभट: mathematics and astronomy
aryabhata.fullTitle: आर्यभट presents computational astronomy and mathematics
aryabhata.define: The concise treatise includes numerical algorithms, a sine table and astronomical models. Its verse format depended on explanation and commentary, and its mathematical contents circulated through subsequent scholarly traditions.
aryabhata.subject: analysis
aryabhata.precision: The text gives an internal chronological reference associated with 499. The chart locates this event by year, not by an assumed 1 January date.

brahmagupta.title: ब्रह्मगुप्त: zero and signed quantities
brahmagupta.fullTitle: ब्रह्मगुप्त sets out rules for zero and signed quantities
brahmagupta.define: Rules for positive, negative and zero quantities formed part of a larger astronomical and mathematical work. His treatment of division by zero was not the modern one; historical progress did not arrive as one complete contemporary system.
brahmagupta.subject: algebra
brahmagupta.precision: Date of the major treatise; distinguish its arithmetic rules from modern conventions. The chart locates this event by year, not by an assumed 1 January date.

khwarizmi-algebra.title: محمد بن موسى الخوارزمي: algebra
khwarizmi-algebra.fullTitle: محمد بن موسى الخوارزمي systematizes algebraic procedures
khwarizmi-algebra.define: A treatise organized linear and quadratic problems into types and justified procedures geometrically. The work helped establish algebra as an identifiable subject, while retaining verbal expression rather than modern equation notation.
khwarizmi-algebra.subject: algebra
khwarizmi-algebra.precision: Approximate composition date in the early ninth century. The chart locates this event by year, not by an assumed 1 January date.

khwarizmi-numerals.title: محمد بن موسى الخوارزمي: positional arithmetic
khwarizmi-numerals.fullTitle: محمد بن موسى الخوارزمي explains calculation with Indian numerals
khwarizmi-numerals.define: A work on positional arithmetic became influential through later translation and adaptation. This was transmission and development of earlier numerical practices, not the first invention of positional notation or zero.
khwarizmi-numerals.subject: algebra
khwarizmi-numerals.precision: Approximate date; the Arabic original is lost and later versions mediate the evidence. The chart locates this event by year, not by an assumed 1 January date.

thabit.title: ثابت بن قرة: geometry and translation
thabit.fullTitle: ثابت بن قرة extends Greek mathematical traditions
thabit.define: Translation and original research addressed number theory, geometry and measurement. His work exemplifies active mathematical transformation in Arabic scholarship, beyond merely preserving earlier texts.
thabit.subject: geometry
thabit.precision: Approximate late ninth-century landmark in a wider career. The chart locates this event by year, not by an assumed 1 January date.

al-battani.title: محمد بن جابر البتاني: astronomical tables
al-battani.fullTitle: محمد بن جابر البتاني improves astronomical computation
al-battani.define: Observations and trigonometric methods refined solar and lunar parameters. Sine-based calculation linked mathematical tables with observational astronomy across later Arabic and Latin traditions.
al-battani.subject: cosmos
al-battani.precision: Approximate period of major observations and tables. The chart locates this event by year, not by an assumed 1 January date.

ibn-haytham.title: الحسن بن الهيثم: mathematical optics
ibn-haytham.fullTitle: الحسن بن الهيثم develops mathematical and experimental optics
ibn-haytham.define: The Book of Optics explained vision through light entering the eye and analyzed reflection and refraction. Its arguments combined geometry, physical reasoning and controlled observations rather than a single modern experimental protocol.
ibn-haytham.subject: fields
ibn-haytham.precision: Approximate composition period, commonly placed in the early eleventh century. The chart locates this event by year, not by an assumed 1 January date.

khayyam.title: عمر خیام: geometric solutions of cubics
khayyam.fullTitle: عمر خیام studies cubic equations geometrically
khayyam.define: A classification of cubic equations used intersections of conic sections to obtain solutions. This addressed algebraic problems through geometry before general symbolic formulas for cubic equations became available in Europe.
khayyam.subject: algebra
khayyam.precision: Approximate composition date. The chart locates this event by year, not by an assumed 1 January date.

latin-translations.title: Arabic algebra enters Latin translation
latin-translations.fullTitle: Latin translation expands access to Arabic algebra
latin-translations.define: A dated Latin translation of the algebraic treatise associated with محمد بن موسى الخوارزمي helped make its procedures available to new readers. Transmission involved selection, translation and local teaching, not a simple transfer between isolated civilizations.
latin-translations.subject: algebra
latin-translations.precision: Translation date; the Arabic work was composed centuries earlier. The chart locates this event by year, not by an assumed 1 January date.

bhaskara.title: भास्कराचार्य: mathematical astronomy
bhaskara.define: His major synthesis treats arithmetic, algebra and astronomical calculation, including sophisticated reasoning about changing quantities. Such passages deserve their historical context rather than an unqualified claim that modern calculus already existed.
bhaskara.subject: analysis
bhaskara.precision: Date associated with the major synthesis. The chart locates this event by year, not by an assumed 1 January date.

fibonacci.title: Leonardo Pisano: a book of calculation
fibonacci.fullTitle: Leonardo Pisano publishes a book of calculation
fibonacci.define: The work presented Hindu-Arabic numerals and commercial and theoretical problems to Latin readers. Its influence was gradual; the publication did not instantly replace all competing systems of calculation.
fibonacci.subject: algebra
fibonacci.precision: First version in 1202; a revised version followed in 1228. The chart locates this event by year, not by an assumed 1 January date.

qin.title: 秦九韶: equations and congruences
qin.fullTitle: 秦九韶 presents numerical and remainder methods
qin.define: The Mathematical Treatise in Nine Sections includes methods for high-degree numerical equations and simultaneous congruences. The surviving work shows algebraic computation embedded in surveying, administration and other practical problems.
qin.subject: algebra
qin.precision: Dated treatise. The chart locates this event by year, not by an assumed 1 January date.

li-ye.title: 李冶: the celestial-element method
li-ye.fullTitle: 李冶 develops the celestial-element method
li-ye.define: Circle-measurement problems are organized through polynomial relations and counting-rod techniques. The work makes explicit the power of an unknown quantity for connecting geometrical conditions to calculation.
li-ye.subject: algebra
li-ye.precision: Date of the treatise on circle measurement. The chart locates this event by year, not by an assumed 1 January date.

zhu.title: 朱世傑: four unknowns and elimination
zhu.fullTitle: 朱世傑 develops multivariable polynomial methods
zhu.define: The Jade Mirror of the Four Unknowns presents elimination and systems involving several unknowns. It represents a sophisticated algebraic tradition whose notation and later transmission differ from European symbolic algebra.
zhu.subject: algebra
zhu.precision: Dated treatise. The chart locates this event by year, not by an assumed 1 January date.

oresme.title: Nicole Oresme: geometry of varying motion
oresme.fullTitle: Nicole Oresme represents changing qualities geometrically
oresme.define: Geometrical configurations described the intensity and extension of variable quantities, including motion. These ideas supported arguments about uniform acceleration without yet providing a modern coordinate system or integral calculus.
oresme.subject: motion
oresme.precision: Approximate mid-fourteenth-century work. The chart locates this event by year, not by an assumed 1 January date.

madhava.title: മാധവൻ: infinite-series methods
madhava.define: The Kerala tradition attributes series for trigonometric quantities and the circle ratio to മാധവൻ. Much evidence comes from later expositions; claims of direct transmission to European calculus require evidence beyond similarity of formulas.
madhava.subject: analysis
madhava.precision: Approximate working date; later texts preserve much of the attribution. The chart locates this event by year, not by an assumed 1 January date.

kashi.title: غیاث‌الدین جمشید کاشانی: circle computation
kashi.fullTitle: غیاث‌الدین جمشید کاشانی calculates the circle ratio
kashi.define: A polygon-based calculation achieved striking sexagesimal precision. This result links computational technique with astronomical requirements and should be distinguished from later infinite-series methods.
kashi.subject: analysis
kashi.precision: Date associated with the treatise on circumference. The chart locates this event by year, not by an assumed 1 January date.

nilakantha.title: നീലകണ്ഠ സോമയാജി: revised planetary models
nilakantha.define: The astronomical synthesis incorporates the Kerala mathematical tradition and revised planetary arrangements. Its geometry was developed in a specific computational setting, not as an anticipation of every feature of later European astronomy.
nilakantha.subject: cosmos
nilakantha.precision: Dated astronomical treatise. The chart locates this event by year, not by an assumed 1 January date.

jyesthadeva.title: ജ്യേഷ്ഠദേവൻ: explanations of Kerala methods
jyesthadeva.define: A Malayalam exposition gives extended reasoning for mathematical and astronomical procedures, including infinite series. It is valuable evidence for methods whose earlier history is partly known through later transmission.
jyesthadeva.subject: analysis
jyesthadeva.precision: Approximate composition date. The chart locates this event by year, not by an assumed 1 January date.

copernicus.title: Mikołaj Kopernik: a heliocentric system
copernicus.fullTitle: Mikołaj Kopernik publishes a heliocentric planetary system
copernicus.define: The mathematical reorganization of planetary motions placed Earth among the moving planets. Circular motions and inherited devices remained, so the book should not be equated with the later elliptical and dynamical account.
copernicus.subject: cosmos
copernicus.precision: Publication year, not the beginning of the author's investigations. The chart locates this event by year, not by an assumed 1 January date.

cardano.title: Cubic and quartic formulas in print
cardano.fullTitle: Girolamo Cardano publishes methods for cubic and quartic equations
cardano.define: The publication brought together results involving Scipione del Ferro, Niccolò Tartaglia and Ludovico Ferrari. Its complicated history illustrates collaborative transmission, contested credit and the limits of a lone-inventor narrative.
cardano.subject: algebra
cardano.precision: Publication year; several methods were discovered earlier. The chart locates this event by year, not by an assumed 1 January date.

bombelli.title: Rafael Bombelli: complex arithmetic
bombelli.fullTitle: Rafael Bombelli develops arithmetic with complex quantities
bombelli.define: His algebra supplied systematic rules for expressions involving square roots of negative numbers. Such quantities could help solve equations with real answers, before their later geometric and analytic interpretations.
bombelli.subject: algebra
bombelli.precision: Publication of the first three books. The chart locates this event by year, not by an assumed 1 January date.

viete.title: François Viète: symbolic algebra
viete.fullTitle: François Viète introduces a systematic symbolic algebra
viete.define: Letters represented known and unknown quantities in a general analytic art. The notation made relationships more general while differing from the symbols and conventions that later became standard.
viete.subject: algebra
viete.precision: Publication landmark. The chart locates this event by year, not by an assumed 1 January date.

gilbert.title: William Gilbert: experimental magnetism
gilbert.define: Experiments with magnets and a spherical model supported the proposal that Earth behaves magnetically. The work distinguished many magnetic and electrical phenomena, although the later unified electromagnetic theory lay far ahead.
gilbert.subject: fields
gilbert.precision: Publication year of the major study of magnets. The chart locates this event by year, not by an assumed 1 January date.

kepler-orbits.title: Johannes Kepler: elliptical orbits
kepler-orbits.fullTitle: Johannes Kepler publishes elliptical planetary motion
kepler-orbits.define: Analysis of observations led to elliptical orbits and the area law for Mars. Mathematical modeling was constrained by precise measurements; the physical explanation through universal gravitation came later.
kepler-orbits.subject: cosmos
kepler-orbits.precision: Publication of the first two planetary laws. The chart locates this event by year, not by an assumed 1 January date.

galileo-telescope.title: Galileo Galilei: telescopic discoveries
galileo-telescope.define: Lunar terrain, many stars and satellites of Jupiter challenged inherited views of the heavens. These observations strengthened new cosmological arguments without by themselves proving every part of a heliocentric system.
galileo-telescope.subject: cosmos
galileo-telescope.precision: Publication year of the telescopic report. The chart locates this event by year, not by an assumed 1 January date.

napier.title: John Napier: logarithms
napier.define: Logarithms converted difficult products and divisions into more manageable arithmetic for astronomical and other calculations. The original construction and scale differed from the later natural and common logarithm conventions.
napier.subject: analysis
napier.precision: First publication. The chart locates this event by year, not by an assumed 1 January date.

kepler-harmonic.title: Johannes Kepler: the third orbital law
kepler-harmonic.fullTitle: Johannes Kepler relates orbital periods and distances
kepler-harmonic.define: The squared orbital period was related to the cube of the characteristic orbital distance. This quantitative regularity became an important target for later dynamical explanation.
kepler-harmonic.subject: cosmos
kepler-harmonic.precision: Publication year of the third planetary law. The chart locates this event by year, not by an assumed 1 January date.

snell.title: Willebrord Snell: a refraction relation
snell.fullTitle: Willebrord Snell derives a refraction relation
snell.define: The sine relation for refraction supported mathematical prediction of light paths. Earlier work by ابن سهل contained a related relation; independent rediscovery and delayed publication complicate priority claims.
snell.subject: fields
snell.precision: Date associated with an unpublished derivation; not a publication claim. The chart locates this event by year, not by an assumed 1 January date.

harriot.title: Thomas Harriot: posthumous algebra
harriot.define: The published work developed equation manipulation and symbolic techniques, including inequality signs. Editorial selection after the author's death matters when separating surviving publication from the broader manuscript work.
harriot.subject: algebra
harriot.precision: Posthumous publication year. The chart locates this event by year, not by an assumed 1 January date.

galileo-dialogue.title: Galileo Galilei: debating world systems
galileo-dialogue.fullTitle: Galileo Galilei stages a debate over world systems
galileo-dialogue.define: A dialogue brought arguments over terrestrial and celestial motion to a broad readership. The subsequent proceedings show how institutional authority, patronage and interpretation shaped the reception of natural philosophy.
galileo-dialogue.subject: cosmos
galileo-dialogue.precision: Publication year; the trial followed in 1633. The chart locates this event by year, not by an assumed 1 January date.

cavalieri.title: Bonaventura Cavalieri: indivisibles
cavalieri.fullTitle: Bonaventura Cavalieri publishes the method of indivisibles
cavalieri.define: Areas and volumes were compared through families of lower-dimensional elements. The method proved powerful but raised questions about rigor that later limit-based and integration theories addressed differently.
cavalieri.subject: analysis
cavalieri.precision: Publication landmark. The chart locates this event by year, not by an assumed 1 January date.

descartes.title: René Descartes: equations and geometry
descartes.fullTitle: René Descartes connects algebra and geometry
descartes.define: The Geometry related geometric constructions to equations and transformed the study of curves. Modern coordinate practice developed through several contributors and should not be projected unchanged into this text.
descartes.subject: geometry
descartes.precision: Publication as an appendix to a methodological work. The chart locates this event by year, not by an assumed 1 January date.

fermat-margin.title: Pierre de Fermat: the marginal conjecture
fermat-margin.fullTitle: Pierre de Fermat records a claim about powers
fermat-margin.define: A famous marginal claim asserted that no positive integer solutions exist for powers greater than two. The surviving story of a lost proof does not establish that a valid general proof was known at this time.
fermat-margin.subject: algebra
fermat-margin.precision: Traditional approximate date of the marginal note; published posthumously in 1670. The chart locates this event by year, not by an assumed 1 January date.

galileo-motion.title: Galileo Galilei: mathematical motion
galileo-motion.fullTitle: Galileo Galilei publishes mathematical studies of motion
galileo-motion.define: The work developed quantitative treatments of acceleration, projectiles and the strength of materials. Idealized mathematical arguments and experimental practices together helped reshape mechanics.
galileo-motion.subject: motion
galileo-motion.precision: Publication year; investigations extended over many earlier years. The chart locates this event by year, not by an assumed 1 January date.

torricelli.title: Evangelista Torricelli: atmospheric pressure
torricelli.fullTitle: Evangelista Torricelli interprets the mercury barometer
torricelli.define: A mercury column and the space above it became evidence in debates about atmospheric pressure and vacuum. The instrument connected physical theory with reproducible changes in height and environment.
torricelli.subject: heat
torricelli.precision: Letter and interpretation landmark; experiments began earlier. The chart locates this event by year, not by an assumed 1 January date.

pascal-fermat.title: Blaise Pascal and Pierre de Fermat: chance
pascal-fermat.fullTitle: Blaise Pascal and Pierre de Fermat analyze games of chance
pascal-fermat.define: Correspondence on the problem of points supplied systematic methods for dividing stakes in an interrupted game. This was an influential episode in probability, not the beginning of all reasoning about uncertainty.
pascal-fermat.subject: probability
pascal-fermat.precision: Dated correspondence. The chart locates this event by year, not by an assumed 1 January date.

huygens-probability.title: Christiaan Huygens: a treatise on chance
huygens-probability.fullTitle: Christiaan Huygens publishes a treatise on chance
huygens-probability.define: The text organized calculations of expectation and gambling problems into a teachable mathematical subject. Later probability would extend well beyond the finite and symmetric situations emphasized here.
huygens-probability.subject: probability
huygens-probability.precision: Publication year. The chart locates this event by year, not by an assumed 1 January date.

boyle.title: Robert Boyle: pressure and volume
boyle.fullTitle: Robert Boyle reports a pressure-volume relationship
boyle.define: Air experiments related pressure and volume under controlled conditions. The empirical relationship applied approximately at fixed temperature; later thermodynamics and kinetic theory supplied broader frameworks.
boyle.subject: heat
boyle.precision: Publication of the experimental relation; the temperature qualification is a modern formulation of its domain. The chart locates this event by year, not by an assumed 1 January date.

hooke-cells.title: Robert Hooke: microscopic observations
hooke-cells.define: Improved instruments made small-scale structures available to public scrutiny through images and descriptions. The work links optical technology, observation and the interpretation of previously inaccessible physical objects.
hooke-cells.subject: fields
hooke-cells.precision: Publication year. The chart locates this event by year, not by an assumed 1 January date.

newton-fluxions.title: Isaac Newton: early fluxions manuscripts
newton-fluxions.fullTitle: Isaac Newton develops early methods of fluxions
newton-fluxions.define: Private investigations connected changing quantities, tangents and quadrature. The development took place over several years, and later publication must be distinguished from the date of manuscript work.
newton-fluxions.subject: analysis
newton-fluxions.precision: Landmark for work during 1665–1666; not public dissemination of a finished calculus. The chart locates this event by year, not by an assumed 1 January date.

newton-light.title: Isaac Newton: light and color
newton-light.fullTitle: Isaac Newton reports experiments on light and color
newton-light.define: Prism experiments supported the claim that white light contains differently refrangible components. The argument reinterpreted color as a property of components of light rather than a simple modification by glass.
newton-light.subject: fields
newton-light.precision: Publication of the optical paper. The chart locates this event by year, not by an assumed 1 January date.

roemer.title: Ole Rømer: a finite speed of light
roemer.fullTitle: Ole Rømer infers a finite speed of light
roemer.define: Timing discrepancies in eclipses of a satellite of Jupiter were interpreted through changing light travel time. The argument connected astronomical observation with a physical property that was difficult to measure terrestrially.
roemer.subject: fields
roemer.precision: Announcement year; later numerical estimates refined the result. The chart locates this event by year, not by an assumed 1 January date.

seki.title: 関孝和: polynomial elimination
seki.define: Work on polynomial elimination and determinant-like expressions advanced Japanese mathematics. Its methods arose within a distinct scholarly and notation tradition, with later comparison to European algebra requiring care about terminology.
seki.subject: algebra
seki.precision: Landmark associated with an early manuscript; not the invention of the modern matrix formalism. The chart locates this event by year, not by an assumed 1 January date.

leibniz-calculus.title: Gottfried Wilhelm Leibniz: calculus in print
leibniz-calculus.fullTitle: Gottfried Wilhelm Leibniz publishes differential calculus
leibniz-calculus.define: A short paper made differential rules publicly available with notation that proved highly influential. Publication chronology and earlier independent manuscript work should remain distinct in discussing the calculus priority dispute.
leibniz-calculus.subject: analysis
leibniz-calculus.precision: Publication year of the differential-calculus paper. The chart locates this event by year, not by an assumed 1 January date.

newton-principia.title: Isaac Newton: motion and gravitation
newton-principia.fullTitle: Isaac Newton unifies celestial and terrestrial mechanics
newton-principia.define: Laws of motion and universal gravitation connected planetary trajectories, falling bodies and tides within a mathematical framework. The achievement relied on earlier observations and mathematics and did not immediately resolve every physical problem.
newton-principia.subject: motion
newton-principia.precision: First edition of the major treatise. The chart locates this event by year, not by an assumed 1 January date.

huygens-light.title: Christiaan Huygens: wavefront optics
huygens-light.fullTitle: Christiaan Huygens publishes a wave account of light
huygens-light.define: A wavefront construction explained reflection and refraction in an assumed medium. Later wave optics retained important geometrical ideas while transforming their physical interpretation.
huygens-light.subject: fields
huygens-light.precision: Publication year; the theory had been presented earlier. The chart locates this event by year, not by an assumed 1 January date.

bernoulli-brachistochrone.title: Johann Bernoulli: the fastest-descent problem
bernoulli-brachistochrone.fullTitle: Johann Bernoulli poses the fastest-descent problem
bernoulli-brachistochrone.define: The challenge asked for the curve of least travel time under gravity. Competing solutions helped make optimization of entire curves a central problem, preparing the ground for the calculus of variations.
bernoulli-brachistochrone.subject: analysis
bernoulli-brachistochrone.precision: Public challenge year; solutions followed in 1697. The chart locates this event by year, not by an assumed 1 January date.

bernoulli-large.title: Jakob Bernoulli: the law of large numbers
bernoulli-large.fullTitle: Jakob Bernoulli's work on probability appears posthumously
bernoulli-large.define: The treatise included a theorem relating observed frequencies to underlying chances under stated assumptions. This established a mathematical form of the law of large numbers, rather than a guarantee about every finite sample.
bernoulli-large.subject: probability
bernoulli-large.precision: Posthumous publication year. The chart locates this event by year, not by an assumed 1 January date.

taylor.title: Brook Taylor: expansion by derivatives
taylor.fullTitle: Brook Taylor publishes a general expansion formula
taylor.define: A method expressed functions through derivatives in a power-series form. Its utility in approximation and differential equations grew through later work on convergence and the conditions under which such expansions are valid.
taylor.subject: analysis
taylor.precision: Publication year. The chart locates this event by year, not by an assumed 1 January date.

euler-graphs.title: Leonhard Euler: the bridges problem
euler-graphs.fullTitle: Leonhard Euler studies the bridges of Königsberg
euler-graphs.define: The impossibility argument reduced a walking puzzle to connections and vertex degrees. This became a foundational example for graph theory, a subject broader than the original geographical problem.
euler-graphs.subject: foundations
euler-graphs.precision: Year associated with the paper's presentation; printed in 1741. The chart locates this event by year, not by an assumed 1 January date.

euler-mechanics.title: Leonhard Euler: analytical mechanics
euler-mechanics.define: Calculus-based methods recast mechanics in a systematic analytical language. This helped move beyond the geometric presentation of earlier dynamics and supported work on both particles and continuous bodies.
euler-mechanics.subject: motion
euler-mechanics.precision: Publication of the mechanics treatise. The chart locates this event by year, not by an assumed 1 January date.

bernoulli-gases.title: Daniel Bernoulli: a kinetic gas model
bernoulli-gases.fullTitle: Daniel Bernoulli models gas pressure through moving particles
bernoulli-gases.define: A mechanical model connected pressure with particle impacts. It was a significant precursor to kinetic theory, though the later statistical framework and experimental support developed over a much longer period.
bernoulli-gases.subject: heat
bernoulli-gases.precision: Publication in a treatise on fluid motion. The chart locates this event by year, not by an assumed 1 January date.

dalembert.title: Jean le Rond d'Alembert: dynamics
dalembert.fullTitle: Jean le Rond d'Alembert formulates a principle of dynamics
dalembert.define: A reformulation related dynamical problems to constrained equilibrium reasoning. It helped organize mechanics and later became part of the foundations of analytical formulations.
dalembert.subject: motion
dalembert.precision: Publication year. The chart locates this event by year, not by an assumed 1 January date.

dalembert-wave.title: The vibrating-string equation
dalembert-wave.fullTitle: Jean le Rond d'Alembert derives the vibrating-string equation
dalembert-wave.define: The problem linked a physical system with a partial differential equation and traveling-wave solutions. Disagreement about allowable initial shapes exposed important questions about functions and mathematical representation.
dalembert-wave.subject: analysis
dalembert-wave.precision: Paper landmark; the vibrating-string debate continued through later publications. The chart locates this event by year, not by an assumed 1 January date.

euler-analysis.title: Leonhard Euler: analysis of functions
euler-analysis.fullTitle: Leonhard Euler organizes analysis around functions
euler-analysis.define: A major introduction to analysis brought functions, infinite series and exponential and trigonometric relations into a systematic presentation. This enlarged the language used to model continuous change.
euler-analysis.subject: analysis
euler-analysis.precision: Publication year. The chart locates this event by year, not by an assumed 1 January date.

lagrange-variation.title: Joseph-Louis Lagrange: variations
lagrange-variation.fullTitle: Joseph-Louis Lagrange develops an analytic variational method
lagrange-variation.define: Correspondence with Leonhard Euler introduced a method for optimizing functionals without relying on particular geometric constructions. Its later role in mechanics illustrates a direct connection between mathematical technique and physical formulation.
lagrange-variation.subject: analysis
lagrange-variation.precision: Early communication landmark; the published development followed. The chart locates this event by year, not by an assumed 1 January date.

bayes.title: Thomas Bayes: inverse probability
bayes.fullTitle: Thomas Bayes's inverse-probability essay is published
bayes.define: The posthumous paper, communicated by Richard Price, addressed inference about an unknown chance from observations. Later Bayesian methods generalize the argument and make explicit modeling choices that are not supplied automatically by the theorem.
bayes.subject: probability
bayes.precision: Posthumous publication. The chart locates this event by year, not by an assumed 1 January date.

coulomb.title: Charles-Augustin de Coulomb: electrical force
coulomb.fullTitle: Charles-Augustin de Coulomb measures electrical forces
coulomb.define: Torsion-balance experiments supported an inverse-square relation for electrostatic force. The relation supplied a quantitative basis for later potential theory and electromagnetic field descriptions.
coulomb.subject: fields
coulomb.precision: Publication of the principal electrical memoirs began in this year. The chart locates this event by year, not by an assumed 1 January date.

lagrange-mechanics.title: Joseph-Louis Lagrange: analytical mechanics
lagrange-mechanics.define: A systematic formulation used generalized coordinates and variational reasoning to handle constrained motion. The work made a shared mathematical structure visible across apparently different mechanical systems.
lagrange-mechanics.subject: motion
lagrange-mechanics.precision: First edition. The chart locates this event by year, not by an assumed 1 January date.

gauss-algebra.title: Carl Friedrich Gauß: polynomial roots
gauss-algebra.fullTitle: Carl Friedrich Gauß addresses the fundamental theorem of algebra
gauss-algebra.define: His dissertation offered a new proof attempt that every nonconstant complex polynomial has a root. Later work strengthened the underlying foundations; historical proofs should not be judged identical to modern presentations.
gauss-algebra.subject: algebra
gauss-algebra.precision: Dissertation year; later proofs and refinements followed. The chart locates this event by year, not by an assumed 1 January date.

gauss-number.title: Carl Friedrich Gauß: number theory
gauss-number.fullTitle: Carl Friedrich Gauß reorganizes number theory
gauss-number.define: A systematic treatment of congruences, quadratic residues and related structures gave number theory a durable research framework. The work brought together earlier results and new proofs rather than beginning the study of integers.
gauss-number.subject: algebra
gauss-number.precision: Publication year. The chart locates this event by year, not by an assumed 1 January date.

young-interference.title: Thomas Young: light interference
young-interference.fullTitle: Thomas Young presents an interference principle
young-interference.define: A wave account connected superposition with the colors of thin films and related optical phenomena. The famous two-slit demonstration is often used to explain the principle, but its later textbook form should not replace the historical sequence of lectures and experiments.
young-interference.subject: fields
young-interference.precision: Lecture landmark; the published lecture appeared in 1802 and further demonstrations followed. The chart locates this event by year, not by an assumed 1 January date.

fourier-memoir.title: Joseph Fourier: the submitted heat memoir
fourier-memoir.fullTitle: Joseph Fourier submits a mathematical theory of heat
fourier-memoir.define: The submitted memoir proposed representing temperature distributions through trigonometric series. Questions about arbitrary functions and convergence generated mathematical debate; publication of the full treatise followed much later.
fourier-memoir.subject: analysis
fourier-memoir.precision: Submission year, distinct from the 1822 book. The chart locates this event by year, not by an assumed 1 January date.

gauss-orbits.title: Carl Friedrich Gauß: orbital estimation
gauss-orbits.fullTitle: Carl Friedrich Gauß publishes methods for orbital estimation
gauss-orbits.define: Least-squares reasoning connected observational error with the determination of celestial orbits. Adrien-Marie Legendre had published least squares in 1805, so this event records a major treatment rather than an exclusive first invention.
gauss-orbits.subject: probability
gauss-orbits.precision: Publication year; priority and unpublished earlier work require separate treatment. The chart locates this event by year, not by an assumed 1 January date.

laplace-probability.title: Pierre-Simon Laplace: probability theory
laplace-probability.fullTitle: Pierre-Simon Laplace publishes an analytical theory of probability
laplace-probability.define: Generating functions, limit methods and inference were organized into an extensive mathematical treatment. Applications to astronomy and error estimation helped link probability with quantitative physical science.
laplace-probability.subject: probability
laplace-probability.precision: First edition. The chart locates this event by year, not by an assumed 1 January date.

fresnel.title: Augustin-Jean Fresnel: diffraction
fresnel.fullTitle: Augustin-Jean Fresnel develops a diffraction theory
fresnel.define: A mathematical wave theory explained diffraction patterns and produced a counterintuitive prediction of a bright central spot behind a circular obstacle. The subsequent experimental confirmation strengthened wave optics without settling later questions about the nature of light.
fresnel.subject: fields
fresnel.precision: Prize memoir submission; examination and experimental discussion continued in 1819. The chart locates this event by year, not by an assumed 1 January date.

oersted.title: Hans Christian Ørsted: current and magnetism
oersted.fullTitle: Hans Christian Ørsted observes a magnetic effect of electric current
oersted.define: A compass needle responded to a nearby current-carrying wire, establishing a concrete connection between electricity and magnetism. The observation opened a new experimental and theoretical field rather than immediately providing a complete electromagnetic theory.
oersted.subject: fields
oersted.precision: Experimental announcement year. The chart locates this event by year, not by an assumed 1 January date.

ampere.title: André-Marie Ampère: forces between currents
ampere.fullTitle: André-Marie Ampère investigates forces between currents
ampere.define: Rapidly following the magnetic-current observation, experiments and mathematical models related electrical currents to mechanical forces. The work laid foundations for electrodynamics while using concepts different from the later field formulation.
ampere.subject: fields
ampere.precision: Initial investigations and announcements; major synthesis followed in 1826. The chart locates this event by year, not by an assumed 1 January date.

cauchy-analysis.title: Augustin-Louis Cauchy: rigorous analysis
cauchy-analysis.fullTitle: Augustin-Louis Cauchy publishes a course in analysis
cauchy-analysis.define: Limits, continuity and convergence received systematic treatment, strengthening the foundations of calculus. Some arguments still relied on assumptions later authors would distinguish more carefully, especially uniform convergence.
cauchy-analysis.subject: analysis
cauchy-analysis.precision: Publication year. The chart locates this event by year, not by an assumed 1 January date.

fourier-book.title: Joseph Fourier: the heat treatise
fourier-book.fullTitle: Joseph Fourier publishes the analytical theory of heat
fourier-book.define: The heat equation and trigonometric expansions linked a physical process with powerful mathematical representations. The work stimulated later analysis far beyond thermal problems, including the study of convergence and function spaces.
fourier-book.subject: analysis
fourier-book.precision: Book publication, distinct from the 1807 submitted memoir. The chart locates this event by year, not by an assumed 1 January date.

abel-quintic.title: Niels Henrik Abel: the limit of radicals
abel-quintic.fullTitle: Niels Henrik Abel proves a limit of radical formulas
abel-quintic.define: A proof showed that a general polynomial equation of degree five cannot be solved by radicals. This is a limitation of a specified class of formulas, not a claim that quintic equations have no roots or cannot be approximated.
abel-quintic.subject: algebra
abel-quintic.precision: Publication of the initial proof; a fuller account followed. The chart locates this event by year, not by an assumed 1 January date.

carnot.title: Sadi Carnot: the ideal heat engine
carnot.fullTitle: Nicolas Léonard Sadi Carnot analyzes heat engines
carnot.define: An ideal reversible cycle made engine performance a theoretical question about temperature and heat transfer. The argument was initially expressed within caloric theory; later thermodynamics retained the structural insight while replacing that physical account.
carnot.subject: heat
carnot.precision: Publication year. The chart locates this event by year, not by an assumed 1 January date.

ohm.title: Georg Simon Ohm: electrical resistance
ohm.fullTitle: Georg Simon Ohm relates current, voltage and resistance
ohm.define: A mathematical treatment of circuits established a relationship between electrical quantities under specified material conditions. The relation is not universal for every device or regime, but became central to circuit theory.
ohm.subject: fields
ohm.precision: Publication of the major treatise. The chart locates this event by year, not by an assumed 1 January date.

brownian.title: Robert Brown: microscopic fluctuations
brownian.fullTitle: Robert Brown reports persistent microscopic motion
brownian.define: Observation of suspended particles documented an irregular motion that was not restricted to living material. A quantitative molecular explanation and decisive measurement came later, so this node records observation rather than proof of atomic theory.
brownian.subject: heat
brownian.precision: Publication describing observations made in 1827. The chart locates this event by year, not by an assumed 1 January date.

green.title: George Green: potential theory
green.define: An essay introduced techniques connecting volume and boundary integrals in electrical and magnetic problems. The mathematics later became important in differential equations, field theory and many other physical applications.
green.subject: analysis
green.precision: Privately published essay. The chart locates this event by year, not by an assumed 1 January date.

lobachevsky.title: Николай Лобачевский: alternative geometry
lobachevsky.define: A geometry denying the usual parallel postulate developed into a coherent alternative system. It challenged the assumption that one inherited geometrical structure exhausted mathematical possibilities for space.
lobachevsky.subject: geometry
lobachevsky.precision: First published exposition; an earlier lecture occurred in 1826. The chart locates this event by year, not by an assumed 1 January date.

dirichlet-series.title: Fourier-series convergence conditions
dirichlet-series.fullTitle: Peter Gustav Lejeune Dirichlet proves convergence results for Fourier series
dirichlet-series.define: Clear sufficient conditions connected a function with its trigonometric expansion. This helped distinguish a formal series manipulation from a justified limiting argument.
dirichlet-series.subject: analysis
dirichlet-series.precision: Publication year. The chart locates this event by year, not by an assumed 1 January date.

galois.title: Évariste Galois: equations and permutations
galois.fullTitle: Évariste Galois connects equations with groups of permutations
galois.define: Work relating the symmetries of roots to solvability established a route to modern algebra. Rejected or unpublished manuscripts and later editing complicate the chronology of recognition and dissemination.
galois.subject: algebra
galois.precision: Early publications and manuscript work; the collected memoirs appeared in 1846. The chart locates this event by year, not by an assumed 1 January date.

faraday-induction.title: Michael Faraday: electromagnetic induction
faraday-induction.define: Changing magnetic conditions produced electrical effects, connecting motion, magnetism and current generation. Later field equations gave a compact mathematical formulation of experimental relationships developed here.
faraday-induction.subject: fields
faraday-induction.precision: Experimental discovery year. The chart locates this event by year, not by an assumed 1 January date.

bolyai.title: Bolyai János: non-Euclidean geometry
bolyai.fullTitle: Bolyai János publishes an independent non-Euclidean geometry
bolyai.define: An appendix to his father's work developed a geometry independent of the parallel postulate. Its appearance alongside independent work elsewhere illustrates simultaneous development without requiring a single chain of direct transmission.
bolyai.subject: geometry
bolyai.precision: Publication of the appendix. The chart locates this event by year, not by an assumed 1 January date.

gauss-weber.title: An electromagnetic telegraph
gauss-weber.fullTitle: Carl Friedrich Gauß and Wilhelm Weber build an electromagnetic telegraph
gauss-weber.define: A working communication link joined quantitative magnetic research with instrumentation. The example shows how physical measurement and practical devices could develop together without reducing either to a simple by-product of the other.
gauss-weber.subject: fields
gauss-weber.precision: Construction landmark. The chart locates this event by year, not by an assumed 1 January date.

hamilton-mechanics.title: William Rowan Hamilton: dynamics
hamilton-mechanics.define: A general dynamical method connected mechanics with earlier work in optics. Its phase-space formulation later supplied important structures for statistical mechanics, quantum mechanics and symplectic geometry.
hamilton-mechanics.subject: motion
hamilton-mechanics.precision: First major dynamics paper; a second followed in 1835. The chart locates this event by year, not by an assumed 1 January date.

dirichlet-primes.title: Primes in arithmetic progressions
dirichlet-primes.fullTitle: Peter Gustav Lejeune Dirichlet proves a theorem on primes in progressions
dirichlet-primes.define: Analysis was used to prove that suitable arithmetic progressions contain infinitely many primes. The result became an important bridge from functions and infinite processes to questions about whole numbers.
dirichlet-primes.subject: algebra
dirichlet-primes.precision: Publication year. The chart locates this event by year, not by an assumed 1 January date.

hamilton-quaternions.title: William Rowan Hamilton: quaternions
hamilton-quaternions.define: A four-dimensional number system allowed multiplication that is not commutative. The construction expanded algebra beyond real and complex numbers and later influenced vector methods and descriptions of rotations.
hamilton-quaternions.subject: algebra
hamilton-quaternions.precision: Discovery and communication year. The chart locates this event by year, not by an assumed 1 January date.

joule.title: James Prescott Joule: work and heat
joule.fullTitle: James Prescott Joule measures the mechanical equivalent of heat
joule.define: Experiments connected mechanical work with heat production through quantitative comparisons. The emerging conservation principle drew on several investigators and measurement strategies rather than one definitive apparatus alone.
joule.subject: heat
joule.precision: Early quantitative report; further experiments refined the value during the 1840s. The chart locates this event by year, not by an assumed 1 January date.

grassmann.title: Hermann Grassmann: an algebra of extension
grassmann.fullTitle: Hermann Grassmann publishes an algebra of extension
grassmann.define: An abstract treatment of multidimensional quantities anticipated parts of linear and exterior algebra. Its early reception was limited; later applications in geometry and physics depended on reinterpretation and new notation.
grassmann.subject: algebra
grassmann.precision: First publication. The chart locates this event by year, not by an assumed 1 January date.

neptune.title: Neptune: prediction meets observation
neptune.fullTitle: Mathematical prediction guides the observation of Neptune
neptune.define: Perturbations of a known orbit supported calculations of an unseen planet's position. The observation demonstrated the predictive power of gravitational modeling while leaving a complicated history of independent calculations and credit.
neptune.subject: cosmos
neptune.precision: Observation year; competing calculations preceded it. The chart locates this event by year, not by an assumed 1 January date.

helmholtz-energy.title: Hermann von Helmholtz: energy conservation
helmholtz-energy.fullTitle: Hermann von Helmholtz states a general conservation principle
helmholtz-energy.define: A physical argument connected mechanical, thermal, electrical and other processes under conservation of energy. The synthesis formed part of a broader contemporary development involving multiple investigators.
helmholtz-energy.subject: heat
helmholtz-energy.precision: Publication year. The chart locates this event by year, not by an assumed 1 January date.

boole.title: George Boole: algebraic logic
boole.fullTitle: George Boole applies algebraic methods to logic
boole.define: Logical relations were represented by a symbolic calculus, opening a new direction for formal reasoning. The system developed further in the 1854 book and should not be identified without qualification with every modern Boolean convention.
boole.subject: foundations
boole.precision: First major logic publication. The chart locates this event by year, not by an assumed 1 January date.

kelvin-scale.title: William Thomson: absolute temperature
kelvin-scale.fullTitle: William Thomson proposes an absolute temperature scale
kelvin-scale.define: A temperature scale grounded in thermal theory aimed to reduce dependence on the properties of a particular thermometer. Its subsequent formulation changed as thermodynamics moved beyond caloric theory.
kelvin-scale.subject: heat
kelvin-scale.precision: Initial proposal; later thermodynamic refinement followed. The chart locates this event by year, not by an assumed 1 January date.

clausius-thermo.title: Rudolf Clausius: thermodynamic laws
clausius-thermo.fullTitle: Rudolf Clausius reconciles heat-engine theory with energy conservation
clausius-thermo.define: A new formulation distinguished conservation of energy from restrictions on the direction of thermal processes. This helped establish the first and second laws as different claims about physical transformations.
clausius-thermo.subject: heat
clausius-thermo.precision: Publication of the foundational thermodynamic paper. The chart locates this event by year, not by an assumed 1 January date.

riemann-complex.title: Bernhard Riemann: complex functions
riemann-complex.fullTitle: Bernhard Riemann develops a geometric approach to complex functions
riemann-complex.define: The dissertation connected complex analysis with surfaces and boundary problems. The resulting viewpoint influenced both abstract geometry and mathematical techniques used in physical field problems.
riemann-complex.subject: analysis
riemann-complex.precision: Doctoral dissertation. The chart locates this event by year, not by an assumed 1 January date.

stokes.title: George Gabriel Stokes: viscous flow
stokes.fullTitle: George Gabriel Stokes analyzes viscous flow and pendulums
stokes.define: A mathematical study related fluid resistance to the motion of small bodies under suitable conditions. Later uses in sedimentation and Brownian motion rely on the assumptions behind the low-speed viscous model.
stokes.subject: motion
stokes.precision: Publication year of the relevant pendulum and fluid-friction paper. The chart locates this event by year, not by an assumed 1 January date.

riemann-geometry.title: Bernhard Riemann: metric geometry
riemann-geometry.fullTitle: Bernhard Riemann proposes a broader geometry of space
riemann-geometry.define: A lecture treated geometry in terms of manifolds and locally varying metric relations. The framework later became essential to gravitation theory, but the lecture itself was a mathematical investigation rather than general relativity.
riemann-geometry.subject: geometry
riemann-geometry.precision: Lecture in 1854; published posthumously in 1868. The chart locates this event by year, not by an assumed 1 January date.

cayley-matrices.title: Arthur Cayley: matrix algebra
cayley-matrices.fullTitle: Arthur Cayley publishes a theory of matrices
cayley-matrices.define: Matrices were treated as algebraic objects with operations and structural identities. Their later role in quantum theory depended on mathematical developments far removed from this original setting.
cayley-matrices.subject: algebra
cayley-matrices.precision: Publication of the memoir on matrices. The chart locates this event by year, not by an assumed 1 January date.

riemann-zeta.title: Bernhard Riemann: zeta and the primes
riemann-zeta.fullTitle: Bernhard Riemann connects prime counting with a complex function
riemann-zeta.define: A short paper related the distribution of primes to analytic properties of the zeta function. Its famous hypothesis remained a conjecture, and the timeline does not present subsequent partial results as a complete proof.
riemann-zeta.subject: algebra
riemann-zeta.precision: Publication year. The chart locates this event by year, not by an assumed 1 January date.

maxwell-distribution.title: James Clerk Maxwell: molecular velocities
maxwell-distribution.fullTitle: James Clerk Maxwell derives a velocity distribution for gases
maxwell-distribution.define: Statistical reasoning described a spread of molecular velocities rather than a single typical speed. The approach helped establish probability as a tool for understanding macroscopic physical behavior.
maxwell-distribution.subject: heat
maxwell-distribution.precision: Publication year. The chart locates this event by year, not by an assumed 1 January date.

maxwell-field.title: James Clerk Maxwell: electromagnetic fields
maxwell-field.fullTitle: James Clerk Maxwell publishes a dynamical electromagnetic field theory
maxwell-field.define: A mathematical field account linked electrical and magnetic processes and identified light with electromagnetic propagation. The compact vector equations familiar today resulted from later reformulation.
maxwell-field.subject: fields
maxwell-field.precision: Publication in 1865; the paper was presented in 1864. The chart locates this event by year, not by an assumed 1 January date.

clausius-entropy.title: Rudolf Clausius: entropy
clausius-entropy.fullTitle: Rudolf Clausius introduces the term entropy
clausius-entropy.define: A state quantity formalized restrictions on heat transfer and transformations. Its later statistical interpretation should be distinguished from this thermodynamic definition.
clausius-entropy.subject: heat
clausius-entropy.precision: Publication landmark for the term and formulation. The chart locates this event by year, not by an assumed 1 January date.

boltzmann-h.title: Ludwig Boltzmann: kinetic irreversibility
boltzmann-h.fullTitle: Ludwig Boltzmann develops a kinetic account of irreversibility
boltzmann-h.define: A transport equation and the H-theorem connected microscopic motion with macroscopic relaxation under statistical assumptions. Later objections exposed the importance of those assumptions and the distinction between typical and logically necessary behavior.
boltzmann-h.subject: heat
boltzmann-h.precision: Publication year. The chart locates this event by year, not by an assumed 1 January date.

dedekind-real.title: Richard Dedekind: constructing real numbers
dedekind-real.fullTitle: Richard Dedekind constructs real numbers through cuts
dedekind-real.define: A systematic account supplied real numbers from ordered rational numbers. This helped separate the foundations of analysis from an unexamined appeal to geometric intuition.
dedekind-real.subject: analysis
dedekind-real.precision: Publication year. The chart locates this event by year, not by an assumed 1 January date.

cantor-uncountable.title: Georg Cantor: uncountable infinity
cantor-uncountable.fullTitle: Georg Cantor distinguishes different sizes of infinity
cantor-uncountable.define: A proof showed that real numbers cannot be listed in the same way as positive integers. The result initiated a systematic theory of infinite sets; the familiar diagonal proof appeared later.
cantor-uncountable.subject: foundations
cantor-uncountable.precision: First uncountability paper, distinct from the 1891 diagonal argument. The chart locates this event by year, not by an assumed 1 January date.

gibbs-equilibrium.title: Josiah Willard Gibbs: phase equilibrium
gibbs-equilibrium.fullTitle: Josiah Willard Gibbs develops thermodynamics of heterogeneous systems
gibbs-equilibrium.define: A mathematical treatment connected equilibrium, phases and chemical potentials. It made thermodynamics useful across mixtures and materials, joining abstract state functions with physical and chemical phenomena.
gibbs-equilibrium.subject: heat
gibbs-equilibrium.precision: First part in 1876; the second appeared in 1878. The chart locates this event by year, not by an assumed 1 January date.

boltzmann-entropy.title: Ludwig Boltzmann: statistical entropy
boltzmann-entropy.fullTitle: Ludwig Boltzmann relates entropy to statistical multiplicity
boltzmann-entropy.define: A combinatorial argument connected macroscopic states with the number of compatible microscopic arrangements. Later notation and interpretation refined this link between probability and thermodynamics.
boltzmann-entropy.subject: heat
boltzmann-entropy.precision: Publication year. The chart locates this event by year, not by an assumed 1 January date.

frege.title: Gottlob Frege: a quantified logic
frege.fullTitle: Gottlob Frege develops a formal logical language
frege.define: A quantified logical system expanded the expressive power of formal reasoning beyond traditional syllogisms. It became central to later foundational debates even though its original notation did not become standard.
frege.subject: foundations
frege.precision: Publication year. The chart locates this event by year, not by an assumed 1 January date.

michelson-morley.title: Interferometry tests ether drift
michelson-morley.fullTitle: Albert A. Michelson and Edward W. Morley report an interferometer result
michelson-morley.define: The experiment did not detect the expected directional effect of motion through a stationary luminiferous ether. Its interpretation developed through several theoretical responses; it was not a stand-alone logical proof of special relativity.
michelson-morley.subject: fields
michelson-morley.precision: Publication of the joint experiment. The chart locates this event by year, not by an assumed 1 January date.

hertz-waves.title: Heinrich Hertz: electromagnetic waves
hertz-waves.define: Experiments produced and detected waves with properties consistent with electromagnetic theory, including reflection and interference. They linked a mathematical prediction to controlled laboratory phenomena.
hertz-waves.subject: fields
hertz-waves.precision: Major publications in 1888; experiments developed during preceding years. The chart locates this event by year, not by an assumed 1 January date.

peano.title: Giuseppe Peano: axioms of arithmetic
peano.fullTitle: Giuseppe Peano presents axioms for arithmetic
peano.define: A symbolic account organized arithmetic through explicit assumptions and inference. Later formal systems adapt these axioms, and their expressive strength depends on the surrounding logical framework.
peano.subject: foundations
peano.precision: Publication year. The chart locates this event by year, not by an assumed 1 January date.

poincare-chaos.title: Henri Poincaré: complex celestial dynamics
poincare-chaos.fullTitle: Henri Poincaré exposes complexity in celestial dynamics
poincare-chaos.define: The revised three-body memoir revealed behavior that resisted simple periodic descriptions. The history includes a serious correction to the prize submission, illustrating how error and revision contributed to a new understanding of dynamics.
poincare-chaos.subject: motion
poincare-chaos.precision: Publication of the corrected memoir, following the 1889 prize. The chart locates this event by year, not by an assumed 1 January date.

cantor-diagonal.title: Georg Cantor: the diagonal argument
cantor-diagonal.fullTitle: Georg Cantor presents a diagonal argument
cantor-diagonal.define: A new proof technique showed that certain infinite collections cannot be enumerated. Later diagonal constructions became central to logic and computability, although their applications require distinct formal arguments.
cantor-diagonal.subject: foundations
cantor-diagonal.precision: Publication year. The chart locates this event by year, not by an assumed 1 January date.

noether-rings-precursor.title: David Hilbert: abstract invariant theory
noether-rings-precursor.fullTitle: David Hilbert develops invariant theory through existence methods
noether-rings-precursor.define: A major paper consolidated work showing the power of abstract existence proofs over explicit computation alone. The approach helped prepare later structural algebra and changed expectations about what counted as an effective mathematical result.
noether-rings-precursor.subject: algebra
noether-rings-precursor.precision: Major invariant-theory paper; the basis theorem had appeared in 1890. The chart locates this event by year, not by an assumed 1 January date.

rontgen.title: Wilhelm Conrad Röntgen: X-rays
rontgen.define: Unexpected penetrating radiation was investigated through its effects on screens and photographic plates. The finding quickly changed experimental physics and imaging while raising new questions about matter and radiation.
rontgen.subject: matter
rontgen.precision: Discovery and first communication year. The chart locates this event by year, not by an assumed 1 January date.

becquerel.title: Henri Becquerel: uranium radiation
becquerel.define: Photographic evidence revealed penetrating emissions without the external illumination initially expected. The observation became a starting point for research on radioactivity rather than a complete explanation of its nuclear origin.
becquerel.subject: matter
becquerel.precision: Discovery year. The chart locates this event by year, not by an assumed 1 January date.

prime-number-theorem.title: The prime number theorem is proved
prime-number-theorem.fullTitle: Jacques Hadamard and Charles-Jean de La Vallée Poussin prove prime-density asymptotics
prime-number-theorem.define: Independent proofs used complex analysis to establish the leading growth rate of the prime-counting function. The theorem gives asymptotic behavior, not an exact formula predicting each prime.
prime-number-theorem.subject: algebra
prime-number-theorem.precision: Independent proof publications. The chart locates this event by year, not by an assumed 1 January date.

electron.title: J. J. Thomson: the electron
electron.fullTitle: J. J. Thomson identifies a universal component of cathode rays
electron.define: Measurements of charge-to-mass behavior supported particles much lighter than atoms. The work transformed the atom from an assumed indivisible unit into an object with internal structure.
electron.subject: matter
electron.precision: Experimental publication year. The chart locates this event by year, not by an assumed 1 January date.

curies.title: Polonium and radium are identified
curies.fullTitle: Maria Skłodowska-Curie and Pierre Curie identify new radioactive substances
curies.define: Investigations of unusually active minerals led to reports of polonium and radium. Chemical separation, measurement and collaboration were essential; the discovery was not immediate isolation of large pure samples.
curies.subject: matter
curies.precision: Announcement year; isolation and characterization continued later. The chart locates this event by year, not by an assumed 1 January date.

hilbert-problems.title: David Hilbert: a mathematical research agenda
hilbert-problems.fullTitle: David Hilbert proposes a research agenda for mathematics
hilbert-problems.define: A list of problems connected algebra, analysis, geometry and foundations. The sixth problem explicitly asked for axiomatization of physical theories, showing that the mathematical formulation of physics was itself an open research program.
hilbert-problems.subject: foundations
hilbert-problems.precision: Congress lecture and published problem list; not all 23 problems were spoken in the lecture. The chart locates this event by year, not by an assumed 1 January date.

planck.title: Max Planck: energy elements
planck.fullTitle: Max Planck introduces energy elements in black-body theory
planck.define: A derivation of the radiation law used discrete energy elements in a statistical argument. The meaning of quantization evolved through later work; this step was not already the full quantum mechanics of the 1920s.
planck.subject: quantum
planck.precision: December presentation landmark. The chart locates this event by year, not by an assumed 1 January date.

russell.title: Bertrand Russell: a set-theoretic paradox
russell.fullTitle: Bertrand Russell identifies a paradox in unrestricted set formation
russell.define: The contradiction exposed a problem with forming a set from any descriptive condition. It helped motivate type theories and axiomatic set theories, rather than showing that all mathematics was inconsistent.
russell.subject: foundations
russell.precision: Discovery year; communication and publication followed. The chart locates this event by year, not by an assumed 1 January date.

lebesgue.title: Henri Lebesgue: measure and integration
lebesgue.fullTitle: Henri Lebesgue develops measure and a new integral
lebesgue.define: A new integration theory enlarged the class of functions that could be handled systematically and improved the treatment of limits. It later became fundamental to probability, functional analysis and mathematical physics.
lebesgue.subject: analysis
lebesgue.precision: Doctoral thesis landmark. The chart locates this event by year, not by an assumed 1 January date.

gibbs-statistical.title: Josiah Willard Gibbs: statistical ensembles
gibbs-statistical.fullTitle: Josiah Willard Gibbs publishes equilibrium statistical mechanics
gibbs-statistical.define: Ensemble methods organized the connection between microscopic descriptions and thermodynamic quantities. The framework made probability distributions over states central to the theory rather than treating one mechanical trajectory as sufficient.
gibbs-statistical.subject: heat
gibbs-statistical.precision: Publication year. The chart locates this event by year, not by an assumed 1 January date.

fredholm.title: Ivar Fredholm: integral equations
fredholm.fullTitle: Ivar Fredholm develops a theory of integral equations
fredholm.define: A general treatment connected solvability with properties of integral operators. Together with related research, it helped create the functional-analytic tools later used for waves, spectra and quantum theory.
fredholm.subject: analysis
fredholm.precision: Publication of the major paper. The chart locates this event by year, not by an assumed 1 January date.

einstein-light.title: Albert Einstein: light quanta
einstein-light.define: A heuristic argument treated light energy as localized quanta and applied it to the photoelectric effect. The proposal went beyond quantized exchange in a material oscillator and remained controversial before later evidence accumulated.
einstein-light.subject: quantum
einstein-light.precision: Publication year; a proposal distinct from later experimental confirmation. The chart locates this event by year, not by an assumed 1 January date.

einstein-brownian.title: Albert Einstein: Brownian motion
einstein-brownian.fullTitle: Albert Einstein derives a statistical theory of Brownian motion
einstein-brownian.define: A quantitative relation connected diffusion and microscopic fluctuations with molecular parameters. It made suspended-particle measurements a route to testing the reality and scale of atoms.
einstein-brownian.subject: heat
einstein-brownian.precision: Publication year. The chart locates this event by year, not by an assumed 1 January date.

einstein-relativity.title: Albert Einstein: special relativity
einstein-relativity.define: A new account of space and time reconciled inertial-frame equivalence with the invariant speed of light. It changed simultaneity and kinematics without including the later theory of gravitation.
einstein-relativity.subject: motion
