einstein-relativity.precision: Publication year of the electrodynamics paper. The chart locates this event by year, not by an assumed 1 January date.

einstein-mass-energy.title: Albert Einstein: mass and energy
einstein-mass-energy.fullTitle: Albert Einstein relates mass and energy
einstein-mass-energy.define: A short argument connected a body's energy change with its inertia. The relationship was developed and generalized through later work; it should not be reduced to a claim that all mass was immediately understood in modern field-theoretic terms.
einstein-mass-energy.subject: motion
einstein-mass-energy.precision: Publication of the separate mass-energy note. The chart locates this event by year, not by an assumed 1 January date.

markov.title: Андрей Марков: dependent random sequences
markov.fullTitle: Андрей Марков studies dependent random sequences
markov.define: Chains with specified transition probabilities extended probability beyond independent trials. The framework later supported statistical physics, stochastic processes and computation, with applications requiring separate modeling assumptions.
markov.subject: probability
markov.precision: Early publication landmark for the chain method. The chart locates this event by year, not by an assumed 1 January date.

minkowski.title: Hermann Minkowski: spacetime geometry
minkowski.fullTitle: Hermann Minkowski presents a spacetime geometry
minkowski.define: Special-relativistic relations were organized into a four-dimensional geometric structure. This viewpoint clarified invariant quantities and helped prepare the mathematical language of later relativistic field theories.
minkowski.subject: geometry
minkowski.precision: Lecture year; the printed account appeared in 1909. The chart locates this event by year, not by an assumed 1 January date.

zermelo.title: Ernst Zermelo: axiomatic set theory
zermelo.fullTitle: Ernst Zermelo proposes axioms for set theory
zermelo.define: Explicit restrictions on set formation sought to preserve useful mathematics while avoiding known paradoxes. The system was an important predecessor of later axiomatizations, not already the final modern formulation.
zermelo.subject: foundations
zermelo.precision: Publication year. The chart locates this event by year, not by an assumed 1 January date.

perrin.title: Jean Perrin: experimental molecular evidence
perrin.fullTitle: Jean Perrin tests molecular theory through particle fluctuations
perrin.define: Measurements of suspended particles supplied quantitative evidence consistent with molecular statistics. Multiple routes to molecular-scale constants strengthened the argument beyond one visual observation of irregular motion.
perrin.subject: heat
perrin.precision: Main experimental landmark; reports and synthesis continued afterward. The chart locates this event by year, not by an assumed 1 January date.

rutherford-nucleus.title: Ernest Rutherford: the nuclear atom
rutherford-nucleus.fullTitle: Ernest Rutherford proposes a concentrated atomic nucleus
rutherford-nucleus.define: Large-angle scattering was explained by concentrating positive charge and most atomic mass in a small region. The model followed earlier experiments and did not yet solve the stability or spectra of atoms.
rutherford-nucleus.subject: matter
rutherford-nucleus.precision: Model publication; the key scattering report preceded it in 1909. The chart locates this event by year, not by an assumed 1 January date.

superconductivity.title: Heike Kamerlingh Onnes: superconductivity
superconductivity.define: The resistance of mercury fell abruptly at very low temperature. This established a new material phenomenon whose microscopic explanation required much later quantum and many-body theory.
superconductivity.subject: matter
superconductivity.precision: Experimental discovery year. The chart locates this event by year, not by an assumed 1 January date.

bohr.title: Niels Bohr: quantized atomic states
bohr.fullTitle: Niels Bohr proposes quantized atomic states
bohr.define: A model combined a nuclear atom with restricted states and radiation frequencies tied to energy differences. It explained important hydrogen regularities but did not supply the general quantum mechanics later needed for more complex systems.
bohr.subject: quantum
bohr.precision: Publication of the atomic-model papers. The chart locates this event by year, not by an assumed 1 January date.

ramanujan.title: ஸ்ரீனிவாச ராமானுஜன் writes to G. H. Hardy
ramanujan.fullTitle: ஸ்ரீனிவாச ராமானுஜன் sends results to G. H. Hardy
ramanujan.define: Correspondence initiated a collaboration that brought remarkable work on series, number theory and partitions to a wider mathematical audience. The event marks contact and recognition, not the beginning of the earlier independent investigations.
ramanujan.subject: algebra
ramanujan.precision: Dated correspondence landmark. The chart locates this event by year, not by an assumed 1 January date.

general-relativity.title: Albert Einstein: general relativity
general-relativity.fullTitle: Albert Einstein presents gravitational field equations
general-relativity.define: The metric structure of spacetime became dynamical and linked to energy and momentum. The theory drew on differential geometry and solved important problems while opening new mathematical and observational questions.
general-relativity.subject: motion
general-relativity.precision: November field-equation papers; earlier formulations differed. The chart locates this event by year, not by an assumed 1 January date.

schwarzschild.title: Karl Schwarzschild: an exact solution
schwarzschild.fullTitle: Karl Schwarzschild finds an exact gravitational solution
schwarzschild.define: A solution for a spherically symmetric vacuum field gave a concrete test of the new equations. The modern physical interpretation of its horizon developed later and should not be assigned fully to the original paper.
schwarzschild.subject: cosmos
schwarzschild.precision: Publication year. The chart locates this event by year, not by an assumed 1 January date.

noether-symmetry.title: Emmy Noether: symmetry and conservation
noether-symmetry.fullTitle: Emmy Noether connects continuous symmetries with conservation laws
noether-symmetry.define: A variational theorem related invariance properties to conserved quantities and clarified issues raised by gravitational theories. Its scope depends on mathematical assumptions; it is more precise than the slogan that every visible symmetry yields a new conservation law.
noether-symmetry.subject: motion
noether-symmetry.precision: Publication year of the invariance paper. The chart locates this event by year, not by an assumed 1 January date.

eclipse.title: The eclipse test of light deflection
eclipse.fullTitle: Eclipse expeditions test gravitational light deflection
eclipse.define: Measurements of star positions near the eclipsed Sun were reported as supporting relativistic light bending. Instrumental uncertainty and data selection matter; later observations provided much stronger tests.
eclipse.subject: cosmos
eclipse.precision: Expedition and announcement year; not the sole or final confirmation of gravitation theory. The chart locates this event by year, not by an assumed 1 January date.

noether-rings.title: Emmy Noether: structural ideal theory
noether-rings.define: A structural treatment emphasized chain conditions and general properties of rings and ideals. This helped make abstract algebra a study of relations and transformations rather than only explicit formulas.
noether-rings.subject: algebra
noether-rings.precision: Publication of the foundational ideal-theory paper. The chart locates this event by year, not by an assumed 1 January date.

banach.title: Stefan Banach: complete normed spaces
banach.fullTitle: Stefan Banach develops complete normed spaces
banach.define: An abstract treatment unified problems involving functions and operators. Such spaces made it possible to transfer arguments between different analytical settings and supplied tools for modern differential equations and physics.
banach.subject: analysis
banach.precision: Publication of the dissertation work. The chart locates this event by year, not by an assumed 1 January date.

friedmann.title: Александр Фридман: evolving universes
friedmann.fullTitle: Александр Фридман derives evolving cosmological solutions
friedmann.define: The gravitational equations admitted universes whose spatial scale changes with time. A mathematical possibility preceded the later consolidation of observational evidence for cosmic expansion.
friedmann.subject: cosmos
friedmann.precision: Publication of the first expanding-universe solutions. The chart locates this event by year, not by an assumed 1 January date.

stern-gerlach.title: Otto Stern and Walther Gerlach: beam splitting
stern-gerlach.fullTitle: Otto Stern and Walther Gerlach observe discrete beam splitting
stern-gerlach.define: A beam of silver atoms split into distinct components in an inhomogeneous magnetic field. Its modern explanation involves electron spin, a concept not yet available to the original investigators.
stern-gerlach.subject: quantum
stern-gerlach.precision: Experimental publication year. The chart locates this event by year, not by an assumed 1 January date.

compton.title: Arthur H. Compton: X-ray scattering
compton.fullTitle: Arthur H. Compton explains shifted scattered X-rays
compton.define: The wavelength shift could be described through energy and momentum transfer between radiation quanta and electrons. The result strengthened the particle-like account of radiation without eliminating wave phenomena.
compton.subject: quantum
compton.precision: Publication year. The chart locates this event by year, not by an assumed 1 January date.

bose.title: সত্যেন্দ্রনাথ বসু: quantum counting
bose.fullTitle: সত্যেন্দ্রনাথ বসু develops a new counting method for radiation
bose.define: A statistical argument counted indistinguishable light quanta in a way that reproduced the radiation law. Albert Einstein extended the method to material particles, opening a route to quantum statistics and condensation predictions.
bose.subject: quantum
bose.precision: Paper and translation year; the material-gas extension followed in 1924–1925. The chart locates this event by year, not by an assumed 1 January date.

de-broglie.title: Louis de Broglie: matter waves
de-broglie.fullTitle: Louis de Broglie proposes waves associated with matter
de-broglie.define: A doctoral thesis related particle momentum to wavelength and connected quantum conditions with wave behavior. Later diffraction experiments tested this hypothesis; the thesis alone was not experimental verification.
de-broglie.subject: quantum
de-broglie.precision: Doctoral thesis year. The chart locates this event by year, not by an assumed 1 January date.

pauli.title: Wolfgang Pauli: the exclusion principle
pauli.fullTitle: Wolfgang Pauli formulates the exclusion principle
pauli.define: A restriction on allowed electron states organized atomic structure and spectra. Its later expression in quantum-field theory and its role in matter stability extended beyond the original spectroscopic argument.
pauli.subject: quantum
pauli.precision: Publication year. The chart locates this event by year, not by an assumed 1 January date.

matrix-mechanics.title: Matrix mechanics takes shape
matrix-mechanics.fullTitle: Werner Heisenberg, Max Born and Pascual Jordan develop matrix mechanics
matrix-mechanics.define: A formulation based on observable transition quantities became a noncommutative algebra of physical variables. Recognizing the role of matrices connected a new physical theory to an existing mathematical language.
matrix-mechanics.subject: quantum
matrix-mechanics.precision: Sequence of papers during 1925, not a single jointly written founding paper. The chart locates this event by year, not by an assumed 1 January date.

schrodinger.title: Erwin Schrödinger: wave mechanics
schrodinger.define: An eigenvalue equation generated quantized energies from wave-like mathematical states. The framework proved related to matrix mechanics, while the physical interpretation of the wave function required further arguments.
schrodinger.subject: quantum
schrodinger.precision: Series of papers in 1926. The chart locates this event by year, not by an assumed 1 January date.

born-rule.title: Max Born: probability amplitudes
born-rule.fullTitle: Max Born proposes a probabilistic interpretation of scattering
born-rule.define: The wave function was related to probabilities of outcomes rather than simply a material wave density. This shifted the role of probability within the theory itself, beyond incomplete knowledge of a classical trajectory.
born-rule.subject: quantum
born-rule.precision: Scattering papers and their correction established the probability-amplitude interpretation. The chart locates this event by year, not by an assumed 1 January date.

fermi-dirac.title: Quantum statistics with exclusion
fermi-dirac.fullTitle: Enrico Fermi and Paul Dirac develop exclusion-based statistics
fermi-dirac.define: Independent treatments supplied the statistical distribution for particles obeying the exclusion principle. The framework became essential for electrons in solids, dense stars and many other quantum systems.
fermi-dirac.subject: heat
fermi-dirac.precision: Independent publications. The chart locates this event by year, not by an assumed 1 January date.

uncertainty.title: Werner Heisenberg: uncertainty
uncertainty.fullTitle: Werner Heisenberg states an uncertainty relation
uncertainty.define: The analysis connected limits on jointly specifying conjugate quantities with the new quantum formalism. Later precise inequalities and debates over measurement distinguish mathematical spread from simplistic claims about defective instruments.
uncertainty.subject: quantum
uncertainty.precision: Publication year. The chart locates this event by year, not by an assumed 1 January date.

matter-diffraction.title: Electron diffraction tests matter waves
matter-diffraction.define: Independent crystal and thin-film experiments found diffraction behavior for electrons. They provided experimental support for the wavelength-momentum relation without turning electrons into ordinary classical waves.
matter-diffraction.subject: quantum
matter-diffraction.precision: Experimental reports by separate groups. The chart locates this event by year, not by an assumed 1 January date.

lemaitre.title: Georges Lemaître: expansion and observations
lemaitre.fullTitle: Georges Lemaître connects cosmic expansion with observations
lemaitre.define: An evolving cosmological model was related to galaxy distances and velocities. The work combined theoretical and observational reasoning before a widely recognized empirical distance-velocity report appeared in 1929.
lemaitre.subject: cosmos
lemaitre.precision: Publication year; later translations affected its reception. The chart locates this event by year, not by an assumed 1 January date.

dirac-electron.title: Paul Dirac: the relativistic electron
dirac-electron.fullTitle: Paul Dirac formulates a relativistic electron equation
dirac-electron.define: A wave equation compatible with special relativity naturally incorporated electron spin and led to new interpretive problems about negative-energy solutions. The later prediction and observation of antimatter were additional steps.
dirac-electron.subject: quantum
dirac-electron.precision: Publication year. The chart locates this event by year, not by an assumed 1 January date.

raman.title: Shifted light scattering in liquids
raman.fullTitle: சந்திரசேகர வெங்கட ராமன் and collaborators observe shifted light scattering
raman.define: A small change in the frequency of scattered light revealed exchanges with molecular excitations. The effect opened a powerful spectroscopic method and connected quantum theory with the internal structure of materials.
raman.subject: quantum
raman.precision: Experimental discovery and reports. The chart locates this event by year, not by an assumed 1 January date.

hub-related.title: Edwin Hubble: distance and recession
hub-related.fullTitle: Edwin Hubble reports a galaxy distance-velocity relation
hub-related.define: An empirical relation supported the emerging picture of an expanding universe. Distances and calibrations were later revised, and the observations belonged to a broader history that included earlier spectra and theoretical models.
hub-related.subject: cosmos
hub-related.precision: Publication year, distinct from prior theoretical work on expansion. The chart locates this event by year, not by an assumed 1 January date.

godel.title: Kurt Gödel: incompleteness
godel.define: Sufficiently expressive, effectively axiomatized consistent systems cannot prove every arithmetic truth, and under suitable assumptions cannot prove their own consistency. These are precise limitations on formal systems, not a general claim that reasoning or mathematical truth is futile.
godel.subject: foundations
godel.precision: Publication year. The chart locates this event by year, not by an assumed 1 January date.

von-neumann-quantum.title: Neumann János: quantum theory in Hilbert space
von-neumann-quantum.fullTitle: Neumann János organizes quantum theory in Hilbert space
von-neumann-quantum.define: A mathematical synthesis treated states and observables through operators and Hilbert spaces. It clarified the shared structure of quantum formulations while leaving interpretive questions and later technical refinements open.
von-neumann-quantum.subject: analysis
von-neumann-quantum.precision: Publication of the mathematical-foundations book. The chart locates this event by year, not by an assumed 1 January date.

neutron.title: James Chadwick: the neutron
neutron.define: Experiments supported an electrically neutral constituent with mass comparable to a proton. The discovery transformed nuclear models and supplied a crucial tool for later studies of nuclear reactions.
neutron.subject: matter
neutron.precision: Experimental discovery year. The chart locates this event by year, not by an assumed 1 January date.

positron.title: Carl D. Anderson: the positron
positron.fullTitle: Carl D. Anderson observes the positron
positron.define: Cloud-chamber tracks supported a positively charged particle with electron-like mass. The observation gave a concrete counterpart to the emerging theoretical account of antimatter.
positron.subject: matter
positron.precision: Observation and first publication; a fuller paper followed in 1933. The chart locates this event by year, not by an assumed 1 January date.

kolmogorov.title: Андрей Колмогоров: axioms of probability
kolmogorov.fullTitle: Андрей Колмогоров axiomatizes probability using measure theory
kolmogorov.define: A systematic foundation represented events and probabilities within a measure-theoretic structure. This unified much existing practice while not determining which probability model describes a particular physical system.
kolmogorov.subject: probability
kolmogorov.precision: Publication year. The chart locates this event by year, not by an assumed 1 January date.

epr.title: The completeness of quantum theory debated
epr.fullTitle: Albert Einstein, Борис Подольский and Nathan Rosen question completeness
epr.define: A joint paper used correlations to argue that the quantum description was incomplete under its assumptions. Later formulations and experiments turned related issues into sharper tests; the original paper did not present a practical faster-than-light signaling method.
epr.subject: quantum
epr.precision: Publication year. The chart locates this event by year, not by an assumed 1 January date.

yukawa.title: 湯川秀樹: a nuclear-force carrier
yukawa.fullTitle: 湯川秀樹 proposes a particle-mediated nuclear force
yukawa.define: A theoretical model related the short range of nuclear forces to a massive exchange particle. The later identification of the pion must be separated from the initial proposal and from the intervening discovery of the muon.
yukawa.subject: matter
yukawa.precision: Proposal year; pion evidence came in 1947. The chart locates this event by year, not by an assumed 1 January date.

church-turing.title: Effective computation and its limits
church-turing.fullTitle: Alonzo Church and Alan Turing formalize effective computation
church-turing.define: Independent formal approaches established limits on decision procedures and helped articulate computability. The equivalence of formal models is mathematical; the claim that they capture all effective human procedures has a different logical status.
church-turing.subject: foundations
church-turing.precision: Publication year of foundational papers; the thesis is distinguished from a theorem. The chart locates this event by year, not by an assumed 1 January date.

fission-observation.title: Barium reveals a nuclear puzzle
fission-observation.fullTitle: Otto Hahn and Fritz Straßmann detect barium after neutron irradiation
fission-observation.define: Chemical evidence from irradiated uranium forced a reconsideration of what nuclear reactions could produce. The experimental report should be distinguished from the subsequent physical explanation of a splitting nucleus.
fission-observation.subject: matter
fission-observation.precision: December findings; the paper appeared in January 1939. The chart locates this event by year, not by an assumed 1 January date.

fission-explanation.title: Lise Meitner and Otto Frisch: fission explained
fission-explanation.fullTitle: Lise Meitner and Otto Robert Frisch explain nuclear fission
fission-explanation.define: A physical interpretation connected the chemical products to a dividing nucleus and a large energy release. Naming both interpretation and experiment makes the distribution of intellectual contributions visible.
fission-explanation.subject: matter
fission-explanation.precision: Explanation and publication year. The chart locates this event by year, not by an assumed 1 January date.

ito.title: 伊藤清: stochastic integration
ito.define: A mathematical calculus for random processes enabled rigorous treatment of stochastic differential equations. Its rules differ from ordinary calculus and later became important in diffusion theory and many applied fields.
ito.subject: probability
ito.precision: Publication landmark for stochastic integration. The chart locates this event by year, not by an assumed 1 January date.

manhattan-impact.title: Nuclear weapons and their human consequences
manhattan-impact.fullTitle: Nuclear weapons transform warfare and scientific responsibility
manhattan-impact.define: The first nuclear test and the atomic bombings of Hiroshima and Nagasaki exposed the destructive consequences of organized nuclear research. The history includes civilian suffering, state secrecy and later debates over scientists' political responsibility.
manhattan-impact.subject: matter
manhattan-impact.precision: Events in 1945; not a technical account of weapon construction. The chart locates this event by year, not by an assumed 1 January date.
manhattan-impact.references: [US Department of Energy: wartime history and consequences](https://www.energy.gov/management/articles/manhattan-project)

qed.title: Renormalized quantum electrodynamics
qed.fullTitle: Renormalized quantum electrodynamics becomes quantitatively predictive
qed.define: Work by 朝永振一郎, Julian Schwinger, Richard Feynman and Freeman Dyson reorganized calculations of interactions between light and matter. Agreement with precise measurements made the theory powerful without implying that every mathematical foundation was thereby settled.
qed.subject: quantum
qed.precision: Landmark for developments during 1947–1949, not a single simultaneous publication. The chart locates this event by year, not by an assumed 1 January date.

shannon.title: Claude Shannon: information theory
shannon.fullTitle: Claude Shannon establishes a mathematical theory of communication
shannon.define: Information and channel capacity became quantities that could be analyzed independently of a message's meaning. The entropy formula has structural connections with statistical physics, but the two uses require careful specification of the underlying model.
shannon.subject: foundations
shannon.precision: Publication year. The chart locates this event by year, not by an assumed 1 January date.

distribution.title: Laurent Schwartz: generalized functions
distribution.fullTitle: Laurent Schwartz publishes the theory of distributions
distribution.define: Generalized functions supplied a rigorous setting for derivatives of nonsmooth objects and idealized sources. They became fundamental tools for partial differential equations and the mathematical language of fields.
distribution.subject: analysis
distribution.precision: First volume of the systematic treatise; the theory had been developed earlier. The chart locates this event by year, not by an assumed 1 January date.

game-theory.title: John Nash: equilibrium in finite games
game-theory.fullTitle: John Nash proves existence of equilibria in finite games
game-theory.define: A fixed-point argument established an equilibrium under specified assumptions about mixed strategies. It joined topology with models of strategic behavior, while not asserting that real participants always find or prefer such an equilibrium.
game-theory.subject: probability
game-theory.precision: Short proof publication; a fuller paper followed in 1951. The chart locates this event by year, not by an assumed 1 January date.

yang-mills.title: 楊振寧 and Robert Mills: non-Abelian fields
yang-mills.fullTitle: 楊振寧 and Robert Mills formulate a non-Abelian gauge theory
yang-mills.define: Local internal symmetry was extended beyond the electromagnetic case. The original physical application was incomplete, but the mathematical structure later became central to the description of fundamental interactions and to geometry.
yang-mills.subject: fields
yang-mills.precision: Publication year. The chart locates this event by year, not by an assumed 1 January date.

parity-proposal.title: 李政道 and 楊振寧 question parity
parity-proposal.fullTitle: 李政道 and 楊振寧 question parity conservation in weak interactions
parity-proposal.define: A critical review showed that assumed mirror symmetry had not been adequately tested in weak processes and proposed experiments. Theoretical questioning and experimental demonstration were distinct contributions.
parity-proposal.subject: matter
parity-proposal.precision: Proposal publication year. The chart locates this event by year, not by an assumed 1 January date.

parity-test.title: 吳健雄 and collaborators: parity violation
parity-test.fullTitle: 吳健雄 and collaborators demonstrate parity violation
parity-test.define: Measurements of beta decay from oriented cobalt nuclei showed a directional asymmetry inconsistent with parity conservation. The experiment overturned an accepted symmetry assumption; its authorship is not represented by the associated prize recipients alone.
parity-test.subject: matter
parity-test.precision: Experimental results published in 1957, following work in late 1956. The chart locates this event by year, not by an assumed 1 January date.

bcs.title: A microscopic theory of superconductivity
bcs.fullTitle: John Bardeen, Leon Cooper and J. Robert Schrieffer explain conventional superconductivity
bcs.define: A many-electron quantum theory used paired states to account for key superconducting properties. Its scope does not automatically include every later family of unconventional superconductors.
bcs.subject: matter
bcs.precision: Theory publication year. The chart locates this event by year, not by an assumed 1 January date.

grothendieck.title: Alexandre Grothendieck: homological methods
grothendieck.fullTitle: Alexandre Grothendieck develops homological methods in algebraic geometry
grothendieck.define: A major paper organized derived functors and related structures in a broad categorical setting. The approach helped make cohomology a portable language for connecting geometric and algebraic problems.
grothendieck.subject: algebra
grothendieck.precision: Publication of the foundational homological-algebra paper. The chart locates this event by year, not by an assumed 1 January date.

laser.title: Theodore Maiman: the ruby laser
laser.fullTitle: Theodore Maiman operates a ruby laser
laser.define: A working device produced coherent optical amplification through stimulated emission. It followed earlier theoretical and microwave developments and enabled new experiments in spectroscopy, precision measurement and light-matter interaction.
laser.subject: fields
laser.precision: First operation year; the patent and priority history is broader. The chart locates this event by year, not by an assumed 1 January date.

lorenz.title: Edward Lorenz: deterministic chaos
lorenz.fullTitle: Edward Lorenz demonstrates deterministic nonperiodic flow
lorenz.define: A simplified convection model displayed sensitive dependence and irregular trajectories. The result made limits of long-term prediction tangible without implying that deterministic equations are random or universally unpredictable.
lorenz.subject: motion
lorenz.precision: Publication year. The chart locates this event by year, not by an assumed 1 January date.

atiyah-singer.title: Michael Atiyah and Isadore Singer: the index
atiyah-singer.fullTitle: Michael Atiyah and Isadore Singer announce the index theorem
atiyah-singer.define: A theorem connected the analytical index of an elliptic operator with topological data. It became a major meeting point of analysis and geometry and later informed quantum-field-theoretic reasoning.
atiyah-singer.subject: geometry
atiyah-singer.precision: Announcement year; detailed proofs and extensions followed. The chart locates this event by year, not by an assumed 1 January date.

quarks.title: Quark and ace models are proposed
quarks.fullTitle: Murray Gell-Mann and George Zweig propose constituent classifications
quarks.define: Independent quark and ace models organized hadrons through a smaller set of constituents. Evidence for the physical parton structure and the later theory of strong interactions must be distinguished from the initial classification proposals.
quarks.subject: matter
quarks.precision: Independent proposal year. The chart locates this event by year, not by an assumed 1 January date.

symmetry-breaking.title: Gauge symmetry breaking: three groups
symmetry-breaking.fullTitle: Several groups develop a gauge-symmetry-breaking mechanism
symmetry-breaking.define: François Englert, Robert Brout, Peter Higgs, Gerald Guralnik, Carl Hagen and Tom Kibble developed related mechanisms for massive gauge fields. Later particle discovery tested the broader framework; the 1964 papers were theoretical proposals.
symmetry-breaking.subject: fields
symmetry-breaking.precision: Multiple papers in 1964, distinct from the 2012 particle observation. The chart locates this event by year, not by an assumed 1 January date.

bell.title: John Bell: testable inequalities
bell.fullTitle: John Bell derives inequalities for local hidden-variable models
bell.define: A mathematical result made assumptions about locality and hidden variables experimentally consequential. A violation constrains that class of models; it does not enable controllable faster-than-light communication.
bell.subject: quantum
bell.precision: Theorem publication year. The chart locates this event by year, not by an assumed 1 January date.

singularity.title: Roger Penrose: a singularity theorem
singularity.fullTitle: Roger Penrose proves a gravitational singularity theorem
singularity.define: Global geometric reasoning showed that trapped surfaces imply geodesic incompleteness under stated conditions. This is a theorem about a classical theory's limits, not a complete physical description of what happens at a singularity.
singularity.subject: cosmos
singularity.precision: Publication year. The chart locates this event by year, not by an assumed 1 January date.

cmb.title: Cosmic microwave background radiation
cmb.fullTitle: Arno Penzias and Robert Wilson report cosmic microwave background radiation
cmb.define: A persistent microwave signal was interpreted alongside cosmological work as relic radiation from an early hot universe. The observation and the accompanying interpretation involved different groups and complementary contributions.
cmb.subject: cosmos
cmb.precision: Publication year of the paired observational and interpretive reports. The chart locates this event by year, not by an assumed 1 January date.

electroweak.title: An electroweak model for leptons
electroweak.fullTitle: Steven Weinberg proposes an electroweak model for leptons
electroweak.define: A gauge framework combined weak and electromagnetic interactions with symmetry breaking. Related work by Sheldon Glashow and عبد السلام formed part of the development; later renormalization and experiments were separate achievements.
electroweak.subject: fields
electroweak.precision: Publication landmark; associated contributions span several years. The chart locates this event by year, not by an assumed 1 January date.

pulsars.title: Jocelyn Bell Burnell: pulsar signals
pulsars.fullTitle: Jocelyn Bell Burnell detects the first pulsar signals
pulsars.define: Repeated radio pulses emerged from a systematic survey and careful scrutiny of unusual data. Their neutron-star interpretation followed; this node records detection rather than assigning the entire discovery to the later prize narrative.
pulsars.subject: cosmos
pulsars.precision: Detection in 1967; the discovery paper appeared in 1968. The chart locates this event by year, not by an assumed 1 January date.
pulsars.references: [Original report of a rapidly pulsating radio source](https://doi.org/10.1038/217709a0)

standard-renormalization.title: Broken gauge theories become renormalizable
standard-renormalization.fullTitle: Gerard 't Hooft establishes renormalizability of broken gauge theories
standard-renormalization.define: A proof made a crucial class of gauge models suitable for controlled quantum calculations. Together with work by Martinus Veltman, it helped turn electroweak unification into a quantitatively testable framework.
standard-renormalization.subject: fields
standard-renormalization.precision: Publication year of the decisive papers. The chart locates this event by year, not by an assumed 1 January date.

renormalization-group.title: Kenneth Wilson: critical phenomena
renormalization-group.fullTitle: Kenneth Wilson develops the renormalization-group account of critical phenomena
renormalization-group.define: Changes of scale organized the behavior of systems near phase transitions and explained why different materials can share critical behavior. The framework connected statistical mechanics with methods also central to quantum field theory.
renormalization-group.subject: heat
renormalization-group.precision: Key publications in 1971; the wider program continued afterward. The chart locates this event by year, not by an assumed 1 January date.

bkt.title: A transition driven by vortex topology
bkt.fullTitle: J. Michael Kosterlitz and David Thouless describe a topological transition
bkt.define: A two-dimensional model exhibited a transition governed by the binding and unbinding of vortices. Earlier work by Вадим Березинский was an essential part of this history, and the result broadened the usual symmetry-breaking picture.
bkt.subject: matter
bkt.precision: Publication landmark following related work in 1971–1972. The chart locates this event by year, not by an assumed 1 January date.

qcd.title: Asymptotic freedom and strong interactions
qcd.fullTitle: Asymptotic freedom reshapes the theory of strong interactions
qcd.define: Independent calculations by David Gross and Frank Wilczek and by H. David Politzer showed how a non-Abelian gauge interaction weakens at short distances. This became a central ingredient of quantum chromodynamics.
qcd.subject: fields
qcd.precision: Publication year of the independent calculations. The chart locates this event by year, not by an assumed 1 January date.

hawking.title: Stephen Hawking: black-hole radiation
hawking.fullTitle: Stephen Hawking predicts radiation from black holes
hawking.define: Quantum-field reasoning in curved spacetime implied thermal radiation associated with black holes. The result joined gravitation, quantum theory and thermodynamics, while astrophysical detection of this radiation remains a separate question.
hawking.subject: cosmos
hawking.precision: Initial announcement in 1974; detailed treatment appeared in 1975. The chart locates this event by year, not by an assumed 1 January date.

four-color.title: A computer-assisted four-color proof
four-color.fullTitle: Kenneth Appel and Wolfgang Haken complete a computer-assisted proof
four-color.define: The four-color theorem was established through a finite reduction and extensive computer checking. The result prompted debate about verification and surveyability, motivating later independent and formal approaches.
four-color.subject: foundations
four-color.precision: Proof announcement in 1976; detailed publications followed in 1977. The chart locates this event by year, not by an assumed 1 January date.

rsa.title: Number theory enables public-key encryption
rsa.fullTitle: Ronald Rivest, Adi Shamir and Leonard Adleman introduce a public-key system
rsa.define: Number-theoretic operations supplied a practical route to public-key encryption and signatures. Security depends on precise assumptions and implementation choices; it is not a theorem that every conceivable attack must factor the modulus.
rsa.subject: algebra
rsa.precision: Public announcement in 1977; the journal paper appeared in 1978. The chart locates this event by year, not by an assumed 1 January date.

quantum-hall.title: Klaus von Klitzing: quantum Hall plateaus
quantum-hall.fullTitle: Klaus von Klitzing measures the integer quantum Hall effect
quantum-hall.define: A two-dimensional electronic system displayed precisely quantized Hall resistance. The result linked material experiments with fundamental constants and later topological explanations.
quantum-hall.subject: matter
quantum-hall.precision: Experimental discovery year. The chart locates this event by year, not by an assumed 1 January date.

feynman-simulation.title: Richard Feynman: quantum simulation
feynman-simulation.fullTitle: Richard Feynman argues for simulating physics with quantum systems
feynman-simulation.define: The difficulty of efficiently representing quantum systems on classical machines motivated a different computational architecture. The argument was a research proposal, not a completed universal practical quantum computer.
feynman-simulation.subject: foundations
feynman-simulation.precision: Published paper based on a 1981 lecture. The chart locates this event by year, not by an assumed 1 January date.

aspect.title: Alain Aspect: changing-analyzer Bell tests
aspect.fullTitle: Alain Aspect and collaborators test Bell inequalities with changing settings
aspect.define: Experiments on correlated photons found results inconsistent with the tested local hidden-variable bounds. Later work addressed remaining experimental loopholes; the history is a sequence of increasingly stringent tests.
aspect.subject: quantum
aspect.precision: Publication of the changing-analyzer experiment. The chart locates this event by year, not by an assumed 1 January date.

tknn.title: Topology explains quantized conductance
tknn.fullTitle: A topological invariant explains quantized Hall conductance
tknn.define: David Thouless, 甲元真人, M. Peter Nightingale and Marcel den Nijs related conductance to a mathematical invariant. The result made topology a quantitative tool for understanding a measured transport property.
tknn.subject: geometry
tknn.precision: Publication year. The chart locates this event by year, not by an assumed 1 January date.

fractional-hall.title: Horst Störmer and 崔琦: fractional Hall states
fractional-hall.fullTitle: Horst Störmer and 崔琦 discover fractional quantum Hall states
fractional-hall.define: Experiments revealed Hall plateaus at fractional values beyond the earlier integer effect. Robert Laughlin's subsequent theory explained how interactions could produce emergent fractionally charged excitations.
fractional-hall.subject: matter
fractional-hall.precision: Discovery in 1982; the explanatory wave function was published in 1983. The chart locates this event by year, not by an assumed 1 January date.
fractional-hall.references: [Nobel research summary on fractional quantum Hall physics](https://www.nobelprize.org/prizes/physics/1998/summary/)

donaldson.title: Simon Donaldson: gauge theory and topology
donaldson.fullTitle: Simon Donaldson applies gauge theory to four-dimensional topology
donaldson.define: Methods from Yang-Mills theory imposed strong restrictions on smooth four-manifolds. A physical field theory thus supplied tools for distinguishing geometric structures that purely topological classification did not settle.
donaldson.subject: geometry
donaldson.precision: Publication of the landmark theorem. The chart locates this event by year, not by an assumed 1 January date.

string-anomalies.title: Anomaly cancellation in superstring theory
string-anomalies.fullTitle: Michael Green and John Schwarz demonstrate anomaly cancellation
string-anomalies.define: A calculation removed a major consistency obstacle for a particular superstring theory. It stimulated a large research program, but mathematical consistency is distinct from experimental confirmation that the model describes nature.
string-anomalies.subject: fields
string-anomalies.precision: Publication year. The chart locates this event by year, not by an assumed 1 January date.

laser-cooling.title: Optical molasses cools atomic motion
laser-cooling.fullTitle: Laser cooling creates optical molasses for atoms
laser-cooling.define: Light forces reduced atomic motion dramatically, supporting new traps and precision experiments. Later sub-Doppler results revealed mechanisms beyond the simplest cooling model.
laser-cooling.subject: quantum
laser-cooling.precision: Landmark experiment; later developments extended and revised the theoretical account. The chart locates this event by year, not by an assumed 1 January date.

high-tc.title: High-temperature superconductivity
high-tc.fullTitle: Johannes Georg Bednorz and Karl Alexander Müller report high-temperature superconductivity
high-tc.define: A copper-oxide material showed superconductivity at temperatures above the established range. The discovery opened a major materials field whose microscopic explanation cannot simply be identified with the conventional theory.
high-tc.subject: matter
high-tc.precision: Initial report year. The chart locates this event by year, not by an assumed 1 January date.

jones-witten.title: Edward Witten: knots and quantum fields
jones-witten.fullTitle: Edward Witten relates knot invariants to quantum field theory
jones-witten.define: A topological field-theory interpretation connected three-dimensional geometry with the Jones polynomial. The physical path-integral argument stimulated rigorous constructions as well as new interactions between mathematics and physics.
jones-witten.subject: geometry
jones-witten.precision: Publication year; the mathematical invariant had been introduced earlier. The chart locates this event by year, not by an assumed 1 January date.

mirror-symmetry.title: Mirror symmetry predicts curve counts
mirror-symmetry.fullTitle: Mirror symmetry predicts counts of rational curves
mirror-symmetry.define: Philip Candelas, Xenia de la Ossa, Paul Green and Linda Parkes used ideas from string theory to calculate enumerative predictions. Subsequent mathematical developments clarified and proved substantial parts of this correspondence.
mirror-symmetry.subject: geometry
mirror-symmetry.precision: Publication year; physical predictions and later proofs are separate stages. The chart locates this event by year, not by an assumed 1 January date.

shor.title: Peter Shor: quantum factoring
shor.fullTitle: Peter Shor presents a quantum factoring algorithm
shor.define: An algorithm showed that a suitable quantum computer could factor integers efficiently in the asymptotic sense. This was a theoretical result, not a demonstration of a machine capable of breaking practical cryptographic keys.
shor.subject: foundations
shor.precision: Conference result in 1994; expanded journal publication followed in 1997. The chart locates this event by year, not by an assumed 1 January date.

wiles.title: The repaired modularity proof is published
wiles.fullTitle: Andrew Wiles and Richard Taylor publish the repaired modularity proof
wiles.define: Two papers established the needed semistable modularity result and completed the proof of Fermat's last theorem. The successful publication followed a 1993 announcement and the repair of a gap, so these dates should not be conflated.
wiles.subject: algebra
wiles.precision: Publication of the completed proof and the companion paper. The chart locates this event by year, not by an assumed 1 January date.

bec.title: Condensation in ultracold atomic gases
bec.define: Groups led by Eric Cornell, Carl Wieman and Wolfgang Ketterle produced and investigated condensates in ultracold atomic gases. The achievement tested and extended quantum-statistical ideas proposed decades earlier.
bec.subject: matter
bec.precision: Experimental realization year; different groups and atomic species were involved. The chart locates this event by year, not by an assumed 1 January date.

acceleration.title: Supernovae reveal accelerating expansion
acceleration.fullTitle: Distant supernovae provide evidence for accelerating expansion
acceleration.define: Two observational collaborations found luminosity-distance behavior consistent with accelerating cosmic expansion. Interpretation relies on cosmological and astrophysical assumptions and does not by itself identify the microscopic nature of dark energy.
acceleration.subject: cosmos
acceleration.precision: Discovery reports in 1998; publications and analyses continued in 1999. The chart locates this event by year, not by an assumed 1 January date.

neutrino-oscillation.title: Atmospheric neutrinos change flavor
neutrino-oscillation.fullTitle: Super-Kamiokande reports evidence for atmospheric neutrino oscillations
neutrino-oscillation.define: A directional deficit supported neutrino flavor change, implying nonzero mass differences. Later solar, reactor and accelerator measurements supplied complementary tests and parameters.
neutrino-oscillation.subject: matter
neutrino-oscillation.precision: Publication year of the atmospheric result. The chart locates this event by year, not by an assumed 1 January date.

perelman.title: Григорий Перельман: Ricci-flow preprints
perelman.fullTitle: Григорий Перельман posts the first Ricci-flow preprint
perelman.define: New tools addressed the formation of singularities in geometric evolution equations. Three preprints in 2002–2003 supplied the program leading to the geometrization and Poincaré results; detailed community verification followed.
perelman.subject: geometry
perelman.precision: First preprint in 2002; later preprints and verification are not compressed into this date. The chart locates this event by year, not by an assumed 1 January date.

graphene.title: Atomically thin graphene is isolated
graphene.fullTitle: Андрей Гейм, Константин Новосёлов and collaborators isolate graphene
graphene.define: Experiments on atomically thin carbon layers enabled direct study of unusual two-dimensional electronic behavior. The achievement concerned isolating and measuring the material, not inventing every prior theoretical model of a carbon sheet.
graphene.subject: matter
graphene.precision: Experimental publication year. The chart locates this event by year, not by an assumed 1 January date.

green-tao.title: Ben Green and 陶哲軒: progressions in primes
green-tao.fullTitle: Ben Green and 陶哲軒 prove long arithmetic progressions in primes
green-tao.define: A transference method showed that primes contain arithmetic progressions of every finite length. The theorem is an existence result, not a claim that every prescribed progression consists of primes.
green-tao.subject: algebra
green-tao.precision: Preprint in 2004; journal publication in 2008. The chart locates this event by year, not by an assumed 1 January date.

formal-four-color.title: Georges Gonthier: formal four-color proof
formal-four-color.fullTitle: Georges Gonthier reports a formally checked four-color proof
formal-four-color.define: A proof assistant checked a reworked argument within an explicit formal framework. This changed how the computational parts could be audited while still leaving trust in the logical kernel and implementation to be understood.
formal-four-color.subject: foundations
formal-four-color.precision: Formal verification completed in 2005; the widely cited exposition appeared in 2008. The chart locates this event by year, not by an assumed 1 January date.

higgs-observation.title: ATLAS and CMS: a Higgs-compatible boson
higgs-observation.fullTitle: ATLAS and CMS announce a new Higgs-compatible boson
higgs-observation.define: Independent collision data showed a new particle near 125 GeV with strong statistical significance. Subsequent measurements tested its properties; the announcement did not by itself settle every detail of the symmetry-breaking sector.
higgs-observation.subject: matter
higgs-observation.precision: Announcement on 4 July 2012; distinguish the 1964 proposals. The chart locates this event by year, not by an assumed 1 January date.

zhang-gaps.title: 張益唐: bounded gaps between primes
zhang-gaps.fullTitle: 張益唐 proves a finite bound on recurring prime gaps
zhang-gaps.define: The result established infinitely many pairs of primes separated by at most a fixed finite bound. It was a breakthrough toward the twin-prime problem, not a proof that infinitely many prime pairs differ by two.
zhang-gaps.subject: algebra
zhang-gaps.precision: Announcement and preprint in 2013; journal publication in 2014. The chart locates this event by year, not by an assumed 1 January date.

flyspeck.title: Flyspeck completes formal verification
flyspeck.fullTitle: The Flyspeck project completes formal verification of the sphere-packing proof
flyspeck.define: A collaborative formal proof checked the mathematical and computational structure behind the three-dimensional Kepler conjecture. Completion of verification is a different milestone from the earlier human-readable proof and its publication.
flyspeck.subject: foundations
flyspeck.precision: Project completion in 2014; the formal-proof paper was published in 2017. The chart locates this event by year, not by an assumed 1 January date.

bell-loopholes.title: Loophole-free Bell experiments
bell-loopholes.fullTitle: Independent experiments perform loophole-free Bell tests
bell-loopholes.define: Different teams closed major detection and locality loopholes together under stated experimental assumptions. The findings strengthened the evidence against local hidden-variable accounts without removing the need to state the assumptions of any test.
bell-loopholes.subject: quantum
bell-loopholes.precision: Experimental publications in 2015. The chart locates this event by year, not by an assumed 1 January date.
bell-loopholes.references: [Original separated-spin Bell-test paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/1508.05949) · [Nobel scientific background on entanglement tests](https://www.nobelprize.org/uploads/2022/10/popular-physicsprize2022.pdf)

gw-detection.title: LIGO detects gravitational waves
gw-detection.fullTitle: LIGO detects a gravitational-wave signal from a black-hole merger
gw-detection.define: Two detectors recorded a coherent signal matching a compact-binary merger. The observation connected relativistic dynamics, numerical modeling and extremely sensitive measurement; the public announcement occurred the following year.
gw-detection.subject: cosmos
gw-detection.precision: Detection on 14 September 2015; not the 2016 announcement date. The chart locates this event by year, not by an assumed 1 January date.

gw-announcement.title: Gravitational-wave discovery is announced
gw-announcement.fullTitle: LIGO and Virgo publish the first direct gravitational-wave detection
gw-announcement.define: The analysis and discovery announcement made the 2015 signal available to the wider scientific community. The publication established a new observational channel while reporting uncertainties and model comparisons.
gw-announcement.subject: cosmos
gw-announcement.precision: Publication and announcement on 11 February 2016. The chart locates this event by year, not by an assumed 1 January date.

sphere-eight.title: Марина Вязовська: sphere packing in 8D
sphere-eight.fullTitle: Марина Вязовська solves sphere packing in eight dimensions
sphere-eight.define: An analytic construction supplied a sharp bound attained by the E8 lattice. The proof combines harmonic analysis and modular forms; it does not solve sphere packing in every dimension.
sphere-eight.subject: geometry
sphere-eight.precision: Preprint in March 2016; journal publication in 2017. The chart locates this event by year, not by an assumed 1 January date.

sphere-twentyfour.title: Sphere packing in 24D is solved
sphere-twentyfour.fullTitle: A collaborative proof settles sphere packing in twenty-four dimensions
sphere-twentyfour.define: Henry Cohn, Abhinav Kumar, Stephen Miller, Данило Радченко and Марина Вязовська extended the method to the Leech lattice. These exceptional-dimensional solutions leave most other dimensions unresolved.
sphere-twentyfour.subject: geometry
sphere-twentyfour.precision: Preprint in March 2016; journal publication in 2017. The chart locates this event by year, not by an assumed 1 January date.

multimessenger.title: A merger observed through waves and light
multimessenger.fullTitle: A neutron-star merger is observed through waves and light
multimessenger.define: Gravitational-wave and electromagnetic observations of the same event connected binary dynamics, explosive astrophysics and cosmic distance measurements. The combined evidence is more informative than treating each instrument's signal in isolation.
multimessenger.subject: cosmos
multimessenger.precision: Event on 17 August 2017; joint results announced in October. The chart locates this event by year, not by an assumed 1 January date.

black-hole-image.title: The first black-hole shadow image
black-hole-image.fullTitle: The Event Horizon Telescope publishes a black-hole shadow image
black-hole-image.define: A global interferometer reconstructed emission around the compact object in M87. The result is an inference from measured correlations and imaging methods, not a conventional photograph of the event horizon itself.
black-hole-image.subject: cosmos
black-hole-image.precision: First image publication in April 2019, using observations from 2017. The chart locates this event by year, not by an assumed 1 January date.

si-redefinition.title: SI units are redefined by constants
si-redefinition.fullTitle: The International System of Units fixes defining constants
si-redefinition.define: The kilogram, ampere, kelvin and mole were redefined through exact values of fundamental constants. Realizing these definitions still requires experiments and uncertainty analysis, linking abstract definitions to practical measurement.
si-redefinition.subject: fields
si-redefinition.precision: Effective on 20 May 2019; the international vote occurred in 2018. The chart locates this event by year, not by an assumed 1 January date.

einstein-tile.title: An aperiodic monotile is exhibited
einstein-tile.define: David Smith, Joseph Samuel Myers, Craig Kaplan and Chaim Goodman-Strauss presented a single shape whose tilings are nonperiodic. The initial hat construction allowed reflections; a later construction removed that requirement.
einstein-tile.subject: geometry
einstein-tile.precision: Preprint year; distinguish the initial hat from the later reflection-free construction. The chart locates this event by year, not by an assumed 1 January date.

top-entanglement.title: ATLAS: entanglement of top quarks
top-entanglement.fullTitle: ATLAS publishes an observation of top-quark entanglement
top-entanglement.define: Spin correlations in top-antitop production supplied evidence of entanglement in a new high-energy setting. The analysis connects quantum-information concepts with collider physics and is distinct from a loophole-free Bell experiment.
top-entanglement.subject: matter
top-entanglement.precision: Nature publication in 2024; the preliminary report and preprint appeared in 2023. The chart locates this event by year, not by an assumed 1 January date.
